body: Once the Etsy shop exists, use Etsy Marketplace Insights as a primary research input where accessible: real Etsy search terms, recent search volume, related terms/trends and listing competition. Use limited free research capacity efficiently; if a paid Etsy tier would materially improve research, present exact cost and expected value for owner approval.
note: re-audited 2026-09-19 after the developer credential was verified by use. Marketplace Insights is a Shop Manager surface, not an API product: none of the nine endpoints this application is authorised for touches it, and the approved personal app does not add one. So the blocker was never the shop's existence and is not the API credential either -- reading Insights means reading a rendered page, which is the browser_vision gate. Parked there rather than released into the ready queue as work nothing can start, which is the third time today that distinction has mattered.
title: Etsy Marketplace Insights as First-Party Demand Oracle

body: Score each micro-market using demand, competition/listing density, quality of current offers, pricing/AOV, season timing, Brambleloop differentiation, machine verifiability, support burden and expected contribution. Explicitly hunt meaningful demand where competitors have weak thumbnails, poor PDFs, no video, confusing instructions, weak branding/bundles, stale aesthetics, limited sizes or recurring complaints.
note: radar/arbitrage.py scores a micro-market on the nine dimensions the requirement names, and an unmeasured dimension leaves the arithmetic and is named rather than being filled with a neutral value that keeps the number's shape and loses its meaning. Each score carries the share of its weight that was measured; below 40% it is reported and never ranked; and markets scored more than 15 points apart in confidence are refused a ranking outright, because a caveat is read once and a ranking is read every week. The requirement's own weakness list is eight items and all eight are now accounted for. Thin media closed 2026-09-19 with the benchmark credential: 413 of 438 observed listings carry fewer than five images. Video and recurring complaints closed 2026-09-20 from endpoints already in the sanctioned allowlist -- the deep audit records has_video per listing, and mjs.reviews reads the shop's reviews weekly and counts recurring themes, counts only, never a review's text, a reviewer or a quotation, with a floor of three because one customer's bad day is not a theme. Deliverable clarity, limited sizes and weak bundles closed the same day: intel/deliverable.py reads the listing description that was already arriving with every catalogue page and nothing was reading, and stores eight booleans -- whether the listing states its format, delivery, extent, contents, stitch terms, finished size, yarn and hook -- and a size count, never the seller's copy, on the same rule the review reader follows. Size is asked only of departments where size is a variable, and a size letter is read only from a clause that says 'size', because a bare s, m or l is one of the commonest characters in a pattern listing and a matcher that read '1200 m' of yarn as a size range would manufacture the weakness it was written to find. A bundle is read from the incumbent's own title. Every one of these is measured only where it has been observed: an unread description is excluded, never counted unclear, because our backlog is not their weakness, and the description backfill reaches unchanged listings for no extra request so the whole map closes on one scan. The two the requirement names that no text can answer -- branding coherence and whether the styling looks like this year -- are reported under needs_vision with what they would need, rather than dropped from the list so it could be called complete. score_observed() closes the other half: score_market() was correct arithmetic that had never been called with anything, which is the same defect as a credential nobody has used. It now feeds the four dimensions first-party observation genuinely supports -- demand from observed favourites, the opening in the incumbents' offers from the weakness hunt, what the market charges from observed prices, and machine-verifiability from the share of the department's observed forms the compiler can build -- which is 52% of the weight, above the floor and comparable across departments because every department is scored from the same source. Demand and price are each a department's median against the strongest department in the one catalogue observed, and are named as relative wherever they surface, because there is no absolute scale for either that this company can reach. Listing density stays unmeasured rather than being taken from a single shop's shelf space; season timing belongs to a chosen occasion; differentiation is a claim about us; support burden and expected contribution need orders. A department with fewer than five observed listings is not scored, because two medians are two sellers' decisions. Remaining: weak branding and stale aesthetics are judgements about rendered pages and photographs and wait on browser_vision. /api/arbitrage?pod= and /api/arbitrage/departments.
title: Search-Arbitrage and Competitive-Weakness Scoring

body: Do not fully engineer the first ideas. Generate roughly 75-100 inexpensive concepts -> research about 40 -> develop stronger commercial/visual propositions for about 20 -> prototype/digital-twin about 10-15 -> fully release only the strongest 5-10. Every stage has a kill gate. Concentrate engineering cost only after commercial evidence improves.
note: creative/funnel.py is the staged tournament with the shape the requirement specifies -- 75-100 -> ~40 -> ~20 -> 10-15 -> 5-10 -- and five refusals that stop it being a queue: survivors plus killed must equal entrants, a stage that kills nothing must declare it examined every entrant (a count short of that is a stage that partly did not happen), a kill cause outside the closed vocabulary aggregates to nothing, and a stage fed below its floor is choosing among whatever happened to be there. A concept cannot join late, stages cannot run out of order, and may_engineer() refuses a concept the tournament has not carried to prototype -- the requirement's opening sentence made mechanical. prospecting.field() fills the wide field by round-robin across every reachable proven-and-unserved arena, so breadth is structural rather than a prompt asking for variety, and the concept_ideation routing task is cheap-tier by routing, not by hope: 100 concepts cost about CA$0.27 against CA$2.52 at the deep tier, which is what the requirement's word 'inexpensive' means. prospecting.tournament() has been run at the specified scale: 80 generated, ideation examined 80 and killed 0, research killed 78 (58 sameness, 20 unverifiable). 58 sameness deaths are not a harsh jury, they are one brief asked twelve times: twelve concepts from one question are siblings by construction, and asking a model for variety does not change what it was asked for. The brief now varies per concept rather than per field -- #106's nine named pairs crossed with #107's nine transformation patterns give 81 structurally distinct questions, walked by a co-prime stride so consecutive concepts never share a pairing, and continued across batches so a slot visited seven times asks eighty-four questions rather than the same twelve seven times. Every cross is built through cross(), so the near-synonym and one-dimension refusals still apply: the variety is generated and it is still checked. The index is a blake2b digest rather than hash(), which is salted per process: the brief used to change on every worker restart while the docstring promised the same arena always asked the same question, which makes any comparison between two runs unreadable. The tournament is a weekly cadence (product_tournament) rather than something somebody runs: it draws its field from the one arena this cycle's wheel picked, which reserves 45% of its slots for Christmas, so the priority programme gets depth rather than a turn and breadth comes from the arena moving between cycles. One arena rather than twelve on purpose -- a field spread across every department puts two or three concepts against each of them, and a benchmark comparison needs more than that to be possible at all. The proposition stage runs the two of its three checks that observation supports. The family test (#111) is deterministic and asks whether the hero's construction reaches enough roles including a cheap one, or whether the collection would have to be forced after the hero exists -- which is exactly when the answer is always yes. The angle check is one-sided on purpose: it refuses a concept whose every word the department uses at all is used by more than 34% of its listings, and it does not endorse one whose words simply do not appear, because an absent word is absence of evidence. Margin is named as not applied rather than run: contribution after platform fees passes every concept, since a digital file has no marginal cost and what decides a pattern's margin is the cost to create it, which is #31. A check that always passes is not a gate. The prototype stage runs too. creative/prototype.py authors a CIR from the concept's form and construction, compiles it, and asks the twin whether the object it describes is the one that was asked for -- no model is consulted, because the gate this stage names is deterministic validation and a test asserts the module never reaches for a gateway. The finished size is the input and the stitch count is derived, which is the direction that cannot produce a 'blanket' 100cm wide and 17cm tall. The gauge is derived from the published band of the yarn the pattern declares, so the defect found in the shipped catalogue the same day -- worsted declared at 16 stitches per 10cm against a published band of 11 to 14 -- is structurally impossible in anything this system authors. Every prototype is worked in one stitch, and that is a correctness requirement rather than a simplification: the first draft alternated single and double crochet under a gauge stated in single crochet, compiled perfectly, and built a 150cm throw the twin measured at 225cm. A CIR that compiles and describes the wrong object is what the twin is for, so the stage asks it and refuses a drift above 20%. A form with no finished size on file is refused rather than sized by guess, and the refusal carries its reason: a graded garment is a size chart rather than a finished size, and the grading that decides where the armhole division goes does not exist yet. Sixteen forms have geometry; six are named as engineering items. The release stage runs too. creative/certification.py presents each prototype survivor to the certificate chain with the three inputs it needs and a concept does not carry: a hero rendered from the digital twin, whose provenance is the company's own arithmetic rather than a photograph -- photographic imagery waits on image_generation and an asset claiming to be one is exactly what asset truth refuses; a listing draft assembled deterministically from the concept's own fields, which cannot claim anything the concept does not say and so cannot trip the policy gate's proof check; and a price that is the median of what the benchmark's own listings in that department charge, the median rather than the mean because one bundle at CA$45 moves a mean and does not move what a shopper expects to pay. A department with no observed price falls back to the pricing floor and says so, because a plausible-looking number would read as evidence. The chain then does what it always did: verified end to end, all ten stages run -- compile, twin, geometry, write, reverse, originality, asset truth, policy, physical test, confidence -- and a certificate granted. A refusal there is the chain working rather than the stage failing, and a test asserts this module has no path that can grant a certificate itself, because a tournament that certified its own survivors would be marking its own homework. All five stages now exist and run when the field reaches them, and each is attempted only when the one before it ran, so an out-of-order refusal cannot bury the real finding under a complaint about ordering. A proposition stage fed below its floor is refused by the funnel and the refusal is reported rather than swallowed, because 'research left too few to reach stage three' is a finding about the field and not about the gate. /api/funnel. The four-stage path is verified by tests/test_prototype.py, which drives concepts through a real compile and twin, and by the production run; the local field double reaches 24 research survivors against proposition's floor of 35, which is a property of the double rather than of the system -- the live run reached 45. Tuning the double until it cleared the floor would have been tuning a fixture and calling it evidence, so the tournament test asserts the invariant instead: every stage appears in exactly one of stages_run or stages_not_run, and a stage that did not run always carries the reason, because an empty reason is the one thing a skipped stage must never be able to say. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: the proposition stage's margin check. A pattern's margin is the price, less platform fees, less the cost to create it amortised over the units it sells -- and #31's attribution now supplies the cost to create, so the only missing term is how many units. That needs sales, which no credential can grant. Running the check without it means running the half that passes every concept, which is what the stage already refuses to call a gate.
title: Product Selection Tournament

body: Where platform rules permit, test truthful concepts/aesthetics on Pinterest, social and owned channels before expensive engineering. Clearly identify concepts and do not imply an unavailable item is a finished purchasable product. Never use fake Etsy listings, fake purchases or fabricated engagement.
note: commerce/preproduction.py prepares a concept post and refuses the ways it can go wrong, because the value and the hazard are the same act: a picture of a thing that does not exist, posted where people buy things, is a pre-order somebody will try to place. A post must say it is a concept in the words a scroller reads rather than in a hashtag at the end, and it is checked as meaning rather than as one blessed sentence, since a rule satisfied by an exact string is a rule somebody routes around by writing a different one. Every phrase that promises a purchase is refused -- shop now, get yours, link in bio, pre-order, available now -- and so is a price, because a number with a currency in front of it is an offer and is the most quietly damaging of them. A concept shown with somebody else's photograph is refused at this door as at every other. The prohibition the owner's directive states outright is structural rather than promised: there is no code path in this module that can author an engagement number, interest comes from a named platform or it is reported unmeasured, and a test asserts the absence by reading the source, because 'we would never' is not a control and the whole category does this. The module's own generated copy passes its own gate, which matters -- a module whose output its gate would refuse is one whose gate gets quietly loosened. Remaining and parked on owned_surfaces: posting needs a site or a Pinterest account nobody has created, so nothing is published; the refusals run anyway, which means they are tested before the day they matter. /api/preproduction.
title: Pre-Production Demand Validation

body: Operate two production queues after core QA stabilizes. FAST LANE: lower-complexity Class A/B products such as ornaments, coasters, mug rugs, selected hats, simple decor and suitable simple amigurumi for rapid learning/search coverage. FLAGSHIP LANE: premium blankets, major collections, selected garments and sophisticated seasonal products for authority, content depth and AOV. Both retain all applicable quality gates.
note: commerce/lanes.py operates both queues. A pod says which queue a product may be considered for and the product's own measurements decide, so a garment cannot be argued into the fast lane by typing one component onto it under a deadline. Flagship is never merely 'not fast': substance is proved (a MEDIUM-or-heavier premium form, or a set of three patterns that holds together, plus real size depth where a pod's buyers are a range of bodies), and a product that is neither simple enough to buy learning rate nor substantial enough to buy authority is routed to neither queue and told why. Both floors are enforced because the fast lane eats the flagship lane one defensible week at a time and a flagship-only catalogue learns four things a year; the mix is a share of making capacity, never a count of products. 'Both retain all applicable quality gates' is structural: the list is the release chain's own CANONICAL_STAGES, and applicable_gates() takes the product and has no lane argument at all -- a test asserts that by signature rather than by example. check_release takes gate runs rather than a set of names that passed, because a verdict computed from the absence of failures passes a chain that never ran. 'After core QA stabilizes' is read from the records (regression corpus and run, certified releases, unresolved halting incidents) and an unread signal is its own refusal; until then one queue, running the same gates. A Class B fast-lane product says out loud that a physical sample sets its wall clock, which is why the trend lane (#291) takes Class A only -- and a test holds #291 at least as strict as this one so it cannot become an exemption in a second costume. /api/lanes.
title: Fast Lane and Flagship Lane

body: As soon as real Market Radar is available, score Christmas micro-markets immediately: ornaments, stockings, tree skirts, blankets, pillows, runners, gift bags, hats, amigurumi, quick gifts and bundles. Select from current evidence. Do not allow infrastructure perfectionism to consume the seasonal making window.
note: seasonal/compression.py is the permanent form of this: Christmas is a named priority programme holding 45% of engineering capacity with a 25% floor, and the mix across make lanes is its runway verdict weighted by how soon each lane closes. That makes the compression automatic -- at 150 days MEDIUM leads, at 120 SHORT, from 75 QUICK, and a lane that retires hands its share to the lanes behind it rather than out of the occasion. The engine may retire a product class and may never stand down the occasion: two refusals enforce it. Departments come from the calendar's own event map filtered by open lanes, so what it names is ornaments, stockings, decor, bags, hats and seasonal gift rather than blankets. When no lane can still be launched the programme moves to merchandising rather than stopping, holding the floor through the fortnight the occasion earns the money, and releases only past the buyer's last practical make date. Recomputed daily by seasonal.sentinel, which raises a P3 when a preparation stream is late. /api/seasonal/compression.
title: Christmas 2026 Strike Team

body: Flagships compete as complete project systems: polished PDF, written instructions, charts, progress visuals, print version, video/tutorial where useful, yarn substitution/colour guidance and version-aware AI pattern support. Price the customer outcome rather than page count.
note: publish/substitution.py answers the question a pattern buyer asks first and nobody else answers -- I cannot get that yarn, what can I use and how much of it -- as arithmetic on this pattern's own gauge and yardage rather than a paragraph somebody wrote, and it refuses in three places rather than guessing. Gauge decides which weights substitute, not the name on the band: weight names are a marketing category with heavily overlapping bands, so a substitute qualifies when the pattern's own gauge sits inside that weight's published Craft Yarn Council band, and a pattern with no gauge gets no guidance at all, because a guide without a gauge is a guess with a table around it. Across fibre classes it gives a direction and no number: quality/physical.calibration_key already learned that cotton and acrylic at the same weight do not use the same length of yarn per stitch, and how much they differ is measured on a swatch, not derived from a table. And the arithmetic is deliberately not the obvious one -- scaling the yardage by the ratio of two weights' lengths per 100g looks right and is wrong, because that ratio is about mass rather than length used; at the same gauge and finished size the stitch count and each stitch's yarn path are unchanged, so the metres barely move and what moves is how many balls they arrive in and how heavy the piece is. The first draft made exactly that error and would have sent a buyer home with half the yarn for a 900 m pattern; the regression test holds the correction. Every figure carries a 15% buy margin, because a pattern that tells somebody to buy exactly enough runs them out in the last row in a dye lot that has gone. Colourway guidance checks contrast on perceived lightness rather than hue, because a thumbnail at mobile-grid scale is very nearly greyscale and two colours of equal lightness merge there however different they look in the hand -- and a colourway nobody has stated in hex is reported unmeasurable, since a colour name is somebody's word for it. The block is rendered into the pattern PDF rather than sitting behind an endpoint nothing calls. It immediately found something: every CIR this system generates declares worsted acrylic at 16 stitches per 10 cm, and the published band for medium yarn is 11 to 14. The PDF says so rather than picking a side, because which number is wrong -- the gauge or the weight -- is decided by a swatch and nothing here has seen one. publish/value_stack.py closes three more of the requirement's list. Progress visuals are milestones rather than decoration: a maker halfway up a blanket is asking whether what is on their hook is what should be on their hook, and a picture they can only agree with does not answer that, so each milestone states the stitch count and the centimetres of fabric that should exist at that row, both of which the twin already knows. The print version is a claim about a printer so it is checked against one: most home printers are greyscale and a chart whose colours differ in hue but not in lightness prints as one flat block, which is the same measurement the thumbnail check makes and therefore the same code -- and where it fails the PDF says to follow the chart's letter cues rather than the shading, which is the difference between a warning and a dead end. And the requirement's closing sentence, price the customer outcome rather than page count, is held by making the forbidden thing unreachable: outcome_price() never receives a page count, so none can enter the arithmetic, and a test asserts the signature and the source rather than trusting a docstring. The price is anchored on the department's observed median and moved by the finished object, the commitment in hours and the support depth, because a price with no relation to what that department charges is a number invented about a market this company has already measured. All three are rendered into the pattern PDF. Every element the requirement makes mandatory is built: the PDF, written instructions, charts, progress visuals, a print version, yarn substitution and colour guidance, version-aware support, and a price computed from the outcome. Video is 'where useful' by the requirement's own words, and where this company cannot make one it is not useful; it is named as unavailable rather than promised, because a listing offering a video it cannot make is the plainest kind of misrepresentation; version-aware pattern support already exists in the concierge, which answers from the exact purchased version (#18). Promoting the gauge-versus-weight inconsistency from a printed note to a release gate is the follow-up, and it would currently stop the whole catalogue, which is the point of doing it deliberately.
title: Premium Value Stack

body: Every flagship should accumulate progressively stronger proof: deterministic validation -> independent reverse compilation -> physical tester examples -> real customer projects/reviews -> repeat purchases. Marketing must distinguish proof levels honestly. Use tester/customer photos only with appropriate permission.
note: quality/proof.py is the ladder the requirement names -- deterministic validation, independent reverse compilation, a physical tester's example, a real customer project, a repeat purchase -- with each rung a query against rows rather than a field anybody can set. Three things make 'marketing must distinguish proof levels honestly' mechanical rather than aspirational. The claim level is the highest *contiguous* rung: a customer photograph arriving before any tester made the thing is real and licenses nothing new, and reporting the highest rung reached in isolation is how a listing ends up claiming a test nobody ran, so the leapfrogged rung is reported rather than averaged away. Language is checked against the level rather than against intention -- check_claim is wired into the policy gate and into certify(), and it is deliberately separate from the existing unsupported-claim patterns, which refuse sentences that are never sayable: 'maker tested' is true the day a tester finishes one and false the day before, and no fixed list tells those apart. And a completed sample that *failed* is evidence and not a proof point, because rung three says the thing came out and a sample that disagreed with the pattern is the most valuable result a sample can produce and the opposite of a proof point. Every rung states what it does not prove as well as what it does, because a ladder that only says what each rung establishes invites the reader to round it up. certify() computes the proof position from its own stages rather than looking it up, which is not circular -- it is the same evidence, and a lookup would read a certificate that call has not issued yet. The permission half is enforced at provenance: tester and customer are permitted asset sources and either without a recorded consent_ref is ASSET_CONSENT_MISSING. A reference rather than a boolean, because somebody has to be able to go and look, and absent consent is not implied consent. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: rungs four and five read False until orders exist, and the key is present rather than absent because a missing key and an unreached rung look identical to a caller and mean completely different things.
title: Proof Stack

body: Build a legitimate creator/tester seeding database with specialty, audience fit, reliability, engagement and permissions. Use it for independent physical proof, finished photos, colour variations, crochet-alongs, disclosed affiliate partnerships and real audience exposure. Never require or purchase dishonest reviews.
note: growth/creators.py is the roster, and most of it is what cannot be expressed rather than what is computed. A collaboration buys work -- a tested sample, a finished photograph, a colour variation, a crochet-along, a post, a tutorial segment -- and the deliverable vocabulary is closed and contains no opinion, so 'never require or purchase dishonest reviews' is unrepresentable rather than discouraged; a review somebody writes afterwards is theirs and nothing here asked for it. An arrangement conditioned on sentiment is refused even when the deliverable is honest, including the one nobody writes down ('we will send the next one if it goes well'). A stated follower count stays a claim with its source, there is no reach projection anywhere in the module and a test reads the source to assert the absence, because fabricated engagement arrives as a spreadsheet more often than as a lie. An engagement rate and the day it was observed travel together or neither is recorded. Permission is scoped: a photograph licensed for the creator's own channel is not licensed for our listing, an expired permission is refused like an absent one, and a permission with no reference is an assertion. Outreach is a commercial electronic message, so it travels on CASL's conspicuously-published-address basis with both of its conditions checked here (published without refusing unsolicited messages, and relevant to that business capacity) while the message requirements are delegated to growth/owned.py rather than restated. The shortlist is ordered by delivered work rather than audience, because the largest following on a roster has delivered nothing until it has, and the reliability threshold is the tester roster's own constant. Its own test caught a real defect: the disclosure check matched 'ad' inside 'made' and passed 'made with a lovely pattern' as a disclosed partnership -- a substring check that approved the exact copy it existed to catch. Tables: creator_profiles and collaborations, whose outcome columns are nullable because an unmeasured result is not a zero. /api/creators. Remaining and parked: the roster is empty and populating it means finding and verifying real people from their public pages, which needs browser_vision; an empty roster is reported as an empty roster and never as a network whose reliability is zero.
title: Creator and Tester Distribution

body: Build owned SEO/Pinterest funnels around useful free motifs, mini patterns, tutorials and tools that demonstrate Brambleloop quality and lead naturally to premium singles/collections. Track visitor -> consented email -> first purchase -> repeat purchase -> collection purchase. Free content must have a commercial job.
note: growth/free_to_paid.py holds the condition that makes free work pay rather than merely cost: every asset names the premium product it leads to and the reason somebody who just used it would want that next, and an asset without both is a giveaway with a marketing story attached -- pleasant to make, which is why a shop ends up with dozens and cannot say what any of them did. 'It leads to the collection' is refused as a hope rather than a job. The expensive refusal is the second: a free mini pattern for an object this company sells does not lead to it, it replaces it, and that failure is indistinguishable from success from the inside because the downloads and saves go up while conversion falls -- so the check is against the catalogue's own slugs rather than against a judgement about how much was given away. The ladder is the requirement's own -- visitor, consented email, first purchase, repeat purchase, collection purchase -- and a rung nobody reached has no conversion rather than a bad one, because 0% from an upstream of zero makes an untried funnel look like a failed one, which is how something nobody tried gets abandoned as something that did not work. A rung larger than the one above it is refused as a counting fault rather than reported as a remarkable funnel. An email is a rung only once it is consented: the count comes from the CASL consent records through growth/owned.py, since an address captured without a basis is not a step toward a purchase but a liability with a growth metric attached. /api/free-to-paid. Remaining and parked: no free work has been made and nothing is published, because publishing to an owned surface needs a site and a Pinterest account nobody has granted; the plan reports an empty funnel as empty rather than as failing.
title: Free-to-Paid Acquisition Engine

body: Treat the first 100 legitimate buyers as a deliberate validation cohort. Track acquisition source, search term where available, product, price, conversion context, support issue, refund, review, repeat purchase and cross-sell. The goal is to discover what real Brambleloop buyers value and which acquisition loops repeat.
note: needs real customers; schema and cohort machinery buildable now
title: First 100 Customers Program

body: Track first product, subsequent purchases, category affinity, time to repeat, AOV and lifetime contribution where platform/data rules permit. Segment owned audiences by demonstrated interest. Optimize customer lifetime contribution, not only single-listing revenue.
note: needs real customers; schema and cohort machinery buildable now
title: Customer LTV and Cohorts

body: Test offers as well as designs: single pattern, pattern+video, mini bundle, complete collection, beginner-support package and seasonal bundle. Measure contribution per visitor and revenue per buyer. A winning design with a weak offer should be fixed before being discarded.
note: commerce/offers.py carries the six offers the requirement names and the sentence with teeth in it: a winning design with a weak offer should be fixed before being discarded, so may_retire() refuses a retirement decision taken on a single offer's evidence -- that is a verdict about a price and a package which has acquired the design's name. The floor is offer *families* rather than a count, because a mini bundle, a collection and a seasonal bundle are one proposition at three sizes and 'we tried three things' would otherwise mean three bundles. An offer with fewer than fifteen buyers did not lose, it did not run, and the refusal says so; the answer in both cases is the cheapest shape the design has not worn yet, which the module names. Both measurements are reported and neither alone, because revenue per buyer is the one that flatters: a CA$28 collection bought by three people looks magnificent beside a CA$6 pattern that converts and loses to it, so the ranking is by contribution per visitor, the only one of the two a cost can be set against. An offer whose figures are unmeasured is listed rather than ranked, because a None sorted as a zero puts the best offer nobody measured at the bottom, which is where things get discarded from. Two of the six cannot be delivered today and are named unavailable rather than quietly priced: nothing in this system can make a video, and a beginner-support package is a promise about answer time that nobody has measured the capacity to keep -- an offer that cannot be delivered is a refund and a review, not a test. /api/offers. Remaining and parked: contribution per visitor and revenue per buyer need visitors and buyers, so no offer has a number yet and the comparison says that rather than reporting every offer as equal.
title: Offer Engineering

body: Build internal baselines by category, traffic source, price band and shop maturity for impressions-to-click, favourites, conversion, refunds/support and contribution per visitor. Do not compare a CA$6 ornament and CA$15 blanket as if they share the same funnel.
note: commerce/benchmarks.py makes a baseline belong to a cell -- category, traffic source, price band and the maturity of the shop when it was measured -- because each of those four moves a funnel on its own. compare() returns the refusal and the axes that differ rather than a caveat, since the failure the requirement names is somebody reading two correct numbers side by side: a CA$6 ornament is an impulse at a price nobody thinks about and a CA$15 blanket is a project somebody decides to start, and the shop-wide average sits between two truths and describes neither -- overall() is reported because somebody will ask and is labelled as not comparable to any cell. A thin cell answers, which makes it more dangerous than an empty one, so below three listings or five hundred impressions the number is not produced at all rather than produced with a caveat nobody re-reads. Every metric states what it needs, and an unmeasured one is absent rather than zero: a refund rate of zero on a shop with no orders is not good performance, and a refund rate computed from three orders reads as 33% and is a rumour, which is distinguished from absence by its own message. Price bands come from what the observed market charges rather than from round numbers, so the boundary falls inside the CA$4-12 cluster; maturity is two counts rather than a judgement. A cell keyed on a typo is refused, because it would fail by looking empty. The vocabularies are now shared: #16's experiment memory keys its context on these price bands and this maturity scale, since a memory keyed on 'under_10' against a benchmark saying '6_to_10' matches nothing and lets every closed question quietly reopen. /api/benchmarks. Remaining and parked: every cell is empty because this company has no listings, no impressions and no orders, and that is reported as no baseline anywhere rather than as a baseline of zero.
title: Conversion Benchmark Engine

body: For target Etsy queries, periodically capture legitimately observable search-result sets and score thumbnail composition, price/sale presentation, social-proof signals, pattern+video positioning, category diversity and Brambleloop differentiation. Treat observed rank as directional/contextual rather than absolute.
note: SERP capture needs the browser/vision capability (same gate as MJs)
title: First-Page SERP Laboratory

body: Record hypothesis, pre-period, treatment, exposure, outcome and confounders. Change one primary variable at a time where practical. Maintain experiment memory so disproven ideas are not repeatedly tested.
note: commerce/listing_tests.py adds the four things a listing test needs on top of the pre-registration discipline growth/experiments.py already holds -- a pre-period, exposure, confounders and one primary variable at a time -- and imports the plan and its verdict rather than restating them. Exposure is the one that matters, and it is this build's recurring defect in a new costume: a listing nobody saw did not fail, it was not tested, and to anything reading the outcome column the two are the same row. The consequence is worse than a wrong verdict, because an unexposed test would write a disproof into the memory and block an idea nobody ever tried -- so an unreadable test writes nothing, durably or otherwise. A multi-variable test is allowed, because a listing does sometimes get rebuilt and 'where practical' is otherwise an invitation never to do it; it simply cannot attribute the outcome to any one variable, and it is remembered as a bundle so it never blocks a clean test of one of them later. A confounder is recorded during the window rather than remembered afterwards, and a confounded window is about something else. Only a causal design may close a question: a disproof is the one verdict that stops future work, so a pre/post disproof is kept as an observation, while a supported result that closes nothing is kept as it is. The memory is a table rather than a list, because 'we tried that last year' is exactly the knowledge a restart loses; a disproof applies to the context that produced it (pod, price band, season, shop maturity) and nowhere else, and it reopens when the caller names which part of the context changed -- a memory that never forgets is a way to stop learning, which is the same failure as no memory arriving from the other side. 'Things feel different now' is refused, because it reopens every question ever closed. /api/listing-tests. Remaining and parked: running one needs a live listing and its impressions, so nothing has been established yet and an empty memory says so rather than reporting that nothing is known.
title: Listing Experiment Discipline

body: Before scaling ads, complete the shop: premium icon/banner, About, policies, sections, coherent thumbnails, clear digital-download expectations, truthful product information and rapid support. Accumulate legitimate tester/customer proof. Never manufacture reviews.
note: commerce/trust.py is the sequence as a gate rather than a checklist: six rungs, each reporting passed, failed or unmeasured, and unmeasured is never counted as passed -- a rung nobody has looked at and a rung this shop has cleared are opposite situations. Proof is counted from rows (passed PhysicalTest, sale LedgerEntry) and record_proof() refuses anything without a row behind it, which is the standing rule against manufactured reviews in mechanical form. may_scale_ads() returns rather than raises, because the answer is no for months and a refusal that reads as an error trains a reader to route around it. /api/trust.
title: New-Shop Trust Accelerator

body: Target response in minutes when automation can safely answer from canonical data. Pattern Help must know the exact purchased version. Measure whether fast support reduces refunds and improves genuine reviews/repeat purchase. Escalate uncertainty instead of hallucinating.
note: support/service.py sets separate targets for a canonical answer (5 minutes) and an escalation (24 hours) and never averages them together, because one number lets a fast automated majority bury the slow escalated minority where the unhappy buyers are; meets_target takes the minimum. An untimed case is counted as untimed rather than dropped, since dropping it measures the cases somebody remembered to time, and a response time cannot be revised. Timings live in the case's existing detail column because the deployed database was created with create_all, which adds tables and not columns. Pattern Help already answers from the exact purchased version (concierge). Remaining and data-gated: whether fast support reduces refunds and improves reviews, which needs orders -- reported unmeasurable with the reason rather than as zero, and parked on the customers gate rather than left in the ready queue. That gate is the one thing in the executor's table nobody can grant: it opens when a stranger buys something, counted from the ledger. /api/trust.
title: Customer-Service Conversion Advantage

body: Use genuine time-bounded sales/coupons/order minimums only when policy-compliant. Measure incremental conversion, AOV and contribution, not merely revenue lift. Avoid conditioning the catalogue to require permanent discounts.
note: commerce/promotion.py holds the three things the requirement asks for. A promotion must end and the end must be a date: past 45 days the discounted price is the ordinary price and the struck-through one is decoration, which is the claim consumer law requires a seller to substantiate, and pricing.check_no_fake_discount already refused the other half -- a was-price this shop never charged. A reduction past 40% is a repricing rather than a promotion. Incrementality is refused without a full-price control, because the discounted arm's conversion rate on its own is a fact about people who were shown a discount, and repeating the promotion on it is exactly how a catalogue learns it cannot sell without one. All three numbers the requirement names are reported -- conversion, AOV and contribution -- and contribution is the one a revenue chart cannot show. Two arithmetic corrections are held as tests. The first version compared the gross full price against the net promo price, which manufactures a contribution loss out of the fee schedule and looks exactly like the divergence this module exists to warn about; it compares net against net now. And the module would otherwise have warned about a danger this business cannot currently have: for a digital pattern the marginal cost of a sale is nearly zero, so revenue and contribution largely move together and both say a discount pays whenever units rise enough to cover the cut. They come apart once a real per-order cost exists -- the flat component of the platform fee, and the cost to create the pattern amortised over the units it sells -- so the module says when the two numbers are telling you the same thing rather than manufacturing alarm. Catalogue dependence is counted from listing rows. Remaining and data-gated: whether anything still sells at full price needs orders, and is reported unmeasurable with the reason, because a catalogue with no sales has no full-price sales either and that is a different finding from one that has stopped having them. /api/promotion.
title: Promotional Science

body: Every flagship should have an owned acquisition counterpart: SEO article/tutorial, Pinterest cluster, video where useful and consented email path. Track assisted conversions. Reduce long-term dependence on Etsy for every visit.
note: growth/owned.py turns #20's email clause from a comment into a control. growth/content.py already carried the right sentence -- express consent required before this is ever sent -- in a detail dictionary, and a comment does not stop a send. CASL governs every commercial electronic message this company will ever send, so the rules are code that refuses: a consent has a named basis, a date and a recorded source, and one with no source cannot be checked by anybody later, which is the only thing that makes it a record rather than an assertion. Express consent lasts until it is withdrawn and withdrawal is final. Implied consent expires on its own -- two years from a purchase, six months from an enquiry -- and that is the part that catches careful senders out, because nothing about an address changes on the day it runs out and a list that is not checking simply carries on. Identification and an unsubscribe are conditions of sending rather than good manners, so a message missing either is refused before it reaches an inbox, and the unsubscribe has to keep working for 60 days and be actioned within 10 business days. The module says plainly that passing the screen is not clearance, which is the wording culture/rights.py uses for the same reason. counterparts() reports which certified products have an owned channel and which have none, because a report listing what exists is an inventory and the useful half is the work; an empty coverage report is not full coverage. owned_share() feeds the traffic_source axis of the anti-fragility rule (#29). Remaining and data-gated: assisted conversions and the owned share itself need visits, and are reported unmeasurable with the reason rather than as zero, because a company with no traffic has no marketplace dependence either and that is not the finding anybody wants recorded. /api/owned.
title: Owned-Audience Compounding

body: Start with small legitimate collaborations and disclosed affiliate arrangements where appropriate. Measure attributable traffic, conversion, usable proof assets and support impact before scaling creator spend.
note: growth/creators.py carries #21's discipline. Seeding starts at zero spend, which is not a compromise -- a digital pattern costs nothing to give, so small legitimate collaborations can begin before any budget exists, and anything above zero is consequential spend the module refuses without the owner. A paid or affiliate arrangement must carry its disclosure in the post the audience actually reads, in words a reader would recognise, rather than in a profile or a linked page. may_scale() is the gate before creator spend grows: three completed collaborations because two is a coincidence, and every outcome measured rather than merely not bad -- attributable traffic, conversions, usable proof assets and support impact. The refusal that matters is the quiet one: a null averages as a zero to anything that averages it, so an unmeasured outcome is named and blocks, because a roster scaled on no bad news is a release passed by the absence of a complaint. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: attributable traffic and conversion need a live listing and real orders. The protocol and its refusals run today, so they are tested before the day they matter.
title: Creator Micro-Seeding

body: When a SKU becomes a statistically credible winner, temporarily reallocate substantial research/creative capacity to understanding WHY: theme, category, technique, low-sew/no-sew, aesthetic, season, price, thumbnail, video, buyer intent and bundle opportunity. Run adjacent controlled experiments without cloning the same product.
note: commerce/replication.py is the protocol, and three refusals carry it. Rank is not credibility: in a catalogue of eleven one product is always the best seller and in a catalogue of three the best seller may have sold twice, so a winner needs thirty orders over four weeks and twice the catalogue median, and until then the correct action is to keep selling it and say nothing about why. A catalogue where nothing else has sold is named as a different and more urgent finding rather than as a winner. Second, a winner normally differs from the field on every dimension at once -- the only no-sew product, the only one at CA$6, the only one photographed in daylight -- and each difference is a complete explanation of which at most one is true; so candidate causes are ranked by contrast rather than by appeal, a dimension where every other product differs is called a story rather than a cause, and a fully confounded winner is reported as confounded with the note that the next product is the experiment. Third, adjacent and not cloned: a proposal that varies only the palette is refused by name, because it sells a little, to the same people, and answers nothing. The reallocation is bounded at 35% of capacity for 45 days and returns on its end date whether or not the question was answered, since an unanswered question is a reason to design a better experiment and not a reason to keep the capacity -- 'temporarily' is doing real work in the requirement, and capacity moved with no end date is a permanent bet on one SKU that nobody decided to make. /api/replication. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: a statistically credible winner needs orders, and no product has one.
title: Bestseller Replication Protocol

body: Learn baselines for CTR, conversion, contribution per visitor, refund/support rate and paid CAC. Weak CTR -> thumbnail/title intervention. Strong CTR/weak conversion -> offer/trust/price. Strong conversion/low traffic -> distribution investment. High sales/high support -> QA before scaling. Learn thresholds from real data.
note: numeric scale/kill framework; thresholds need real baselines
title: Numeric Scale/Kill Framework

body: Make Revenue per Visitor and Contribution per Visitor first-class metrics. A higher-priced product with slightly lower conversion may be commercially superior to a cheap product. Pricing, SEO and paid-media agents optimize contribution economics rather than conversion rate alone.
note: scale/runrate.per_visitor() ranks on contribution per visitor and reports when the conversion-rate ranking disagrees, which is the case the requirement exists for
title: Revenue and Contribution per Visitor

body: Express CA$3,000/month as solvable funnel math: e.g. 200 orders x CA$15 AOV, 150 x CA$20, or 120 x CA$25. Then derive required qualified visits from observed conversion. Every weekly review identifies the largest constraint: traffic, CTR, conversion, AOV, repeat rate, product coverage or margin.
note: runrate.decompose() shows the target at four price points and derives required visits only from an observed conversion rate; constraint() names the single binding term, walked in funnel order
title: $3K Run-Rate Decomposition

body: Once enough real data exists, run nightly scenario analysis using listing count, qualified traffic, CTR, conversion, AOV, repeat rate, organic growth, paid CAC, product velocity, winner rate and retirement rate. Show assumptions/sensitivity and identify the primary constraint. Do not present modeled probabilities as objective truth.
note: scale/trajectory.py models the eleven terms the requirement names, and its last sentence governs the module rather than being appended to it. A Monte Carlo over inputs nobody has measured produces a distribution of *assumptions*, not of outcomes, and it produces it to four decimal places with a histogram, which is exactly what makes it persuasive. So no function here returns a bare probability: a number like 0.62 detaches from its provenance the moment somebody writes it in a summary, and a modelled probability without its provenance is the objective-truth claim the requirement forbids. Every figure comes back inside how much of the model was observed, which terms were assumed and on what basis. Below a 60% observed share the run is named an assumption space and states no probability at all, which is the honest form of 'once enough real data exists'; today that share is zero. A term left out of the inputs is refused rather than assumed silently, a point outside its own range is refused as a typo that answers confidently, and a value with no source is refused because it cannot be told apart from a measurement. The sensitivity ranking is the module's real output while the inputs are assumed: it does not say what will happen, it says which assumption the answer is hostage to, which is the one question a company with no data can act on. The seed is the date, so two reads of the same night agree -- the first thing anybody does with a nightly number is compare it to last night's, and a simulator that moves on its own makes that comparison meaningless. The nightly entry point refuses today and names the primary constraint anyway, because 'nobody is arriving' does not need a simulation. /api/trajectory. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: every term needs impressions, visits and orders that do not exist.
title: CA$3K Trajectory / Monte Carlo Simulator

body: Brambleloop may only report 75-90% modeled confidence of reaching/sustaining CA$3,000/month when evidence includes multiple independently selling SKUs rather than one viral outlier; positive contribution margin; stable pattern-quality/support metrics; repeatable qualified traffic; observed conversion over meaningful samples; at least one repeatable acquisition channel; improving legitimate review/trust base; no platform-policy warnings; and a scenario model whose conservative assumptions still approach the target.
note: the evidence gate now carries #27's eight qualitative conditions alongside the counts, and an unstated condition is unmet rather than unknown. Sixty orders from one viral listing satisfies every count and no condition
title: 75-90% Confidence Gate

body: Strong conversion + low traffic -> increase distribution. High traffic + weak CTR -> thumbnail/title. Strong CTR + weak conversion -> offer/trust/price. Sustainable paid CAC below allowable CAC -> scale gradually. Rising support/refund defects -> stop scaling and investigate.
note: runrate.SCALE_RULES holds #28's five conditions as data, constraint() selects one, and rising defects outrank every commercial term
title: Conditional Scale Rules

body: Do not allow one SKU, one holiday, one traffic source, one AI provider or one marketplace to become an existential dependency. Diversify after a channel/product is understood, without spreading resources so thin that nothing gets enough focus.
note: scale/dependency.py implements both halves of the rule, and the second half is the one a concentration report usually forgets. #29 says do not let one SKU, holiday, traffic source, AI provider or marketplace become existential -- and also to diversify *after* a channel or product is understood, without spreading resources so thin that nothing gets enough focus. A module that implemented only the first half would tell a pre-revenue company with one department to open a second marketplace, which is how its one real advantage becomes five half-built ones. So concentration alone is not a finding: a dependency is existential when it is concentrated AND load-bearing, and before it carries anything it is a plan. Every axis reports how concentrated it is, whether it currently carries value, and which of those two facts decided the verdict. Two holders is still concentrated however even the split, because a 50/50 pair passes a share test and is one failure from total. An empty axis is unmeasurable with the reason rather than a comfortable zero -- 'no traffic source is dominant' is true of a company with no traffic and is the most misleading sentence such a company could publish about itself -- and zero configured model providers reports that nothing needing judgement can run at all, which is a different and worse state than concentration. Holders per validated product is the counter-rule, checked rather than remembered, and it reports undefined rather than fine when there are no validated products, because False there would read as 'the spread is within what the catalogue supports' for the most spread-too-thin a company can be. Today: ai_provider is genuinely existential -- one provider at 100% and nothing in this system that needs judgement runs without it; sku is 100% home_decor and concentrated but not yet load-bearing; occasion is sound; traffic_source and marketplace are unmeasurable because nothing is published. Remaining and data-gated: three of the five axes only become load-bearing once there is revenue, and the module names which and what would make them count. /api/dependency.
title: Anti-Fragility Rule

body: After core engineering stabilizes, prevent endless technical polishing from starving distribution. Mature-state conceptual allocation: roughly 30% product/QA, 30% market intelligence/product selection, 30% distribution/growth and 10% infrastructure/operations, dynamically adjusted to the current bottleneck.
note: scale/allocation.py holds the requirement's numbers -- 30% product and QA, 30% market intelligence and product selection, 30% distribution and growth, 10% infrastructure -- and the reason they need enforcing. Engineering work is always available, always visible, always finishes and never requires anybody outside this company; distribution requires an audience that does not exist yet and every hour of it can be defensibly deferred until the thing being distributed is better. A shop can be improved indefinitely and shown to nobody, and at no point does a week feel wasted. So the mature mix is the default rather than the reward, distribution has a floor no bottleneck may cross, and infrastructure has a ceiling because the platform is how the work happens and is not the work. 'Dynamically adjusted to the current bottleneck' reads scale/runrate.py's constraint verdict, and an unmeasured bottleneck is not a bottleneck: guessing does not produce a random answer, it produces whichever term somebody has a benchmark for, which is the one nearest the code. Each mapped term names the function that can actually move it and why, so a tilt cannot become 'whatever we were going to do anyway', and a term the map does not carry is refused rather than absorbed. The tilt takes from whoever can spare it most rather than from whoever is listed first. 'After core engineering stabilizes' is the same evidence #5 reads, imported rather than restated, because two definitions of stable is one definition and one excuse; before then the build mix applies, and it keeps distribution at its floor too, since the starvation this requirement prevents begins before there is an audience. The module's own first draft put the build mix's distribution at 15% against that floor while its docstring claimed the floor was respected -- the slide, written by the module that exists to stop it -- and the invariant test that every shipped mix passes its own check is what caught it. It is a weekly cadence (capacity_review -> ops.capacity) rather than a function somebody remembers to call, on the same reasoning #292 applies to the re-merchandising review: a module nobody calls is precisely 'whatever was easiest to pick up', which is the thing this requirement prevents. The handler is run end to end by its own test, because a handler whose interesting half no test executes is an untested handler with a passing test beside it, and this build has shipped that twice. GREEN: it reads records, writes an audit row, changes nothing and spends nothing. /api/allocation.
title: Growth Resource Allocation

body: Track agent/API minutes and dollar cost per concept, validated pattern, PDF, listing, video asset, support case and acquired customer. Optimize validated products per operating dollar and contribution profit per operating dollar. A six-figure store that burns more than it earns is failure.
note: finance/unit_cost.py reports both of #31's ratios -- validated products per operating dollar and contribution per operating dollar -- and marks artefacts produced by uncosted work as a floor rather than as cheap. The attribution that made those ratios real landed 2026-09-20: registry.record_cost had always accepted a job id and ModelGateway simply never passed one, so every model cost reached the ledger with a null job, unit_costs() could match none of them to the audit row that produced a pattern or a listing, and every artefact reported a floor while the money was real and counted. Correct arithmetic over an empty attribution, which is the same shape as a scorer nobody feeds. An artefact may now be produced by more than one kind of work -- a concept arrives from scoring, from an expedition and from a tournament, and naming one action would quietly cost only the concepts that came the way somebody listed first -- and an artefact whose count lives in the row rather than one-per-row is counted from the row: a discovery run is a single audit entry that produced eighty concepts, and calling it one concept would report a field at eighty times its unit cost, which reads as a reason to stop doing discovery. A job's cost is attributed once, so two artefacts sharing a job cannot each claim the whole of it and push attributed spend above what was spent. The same day found three disagreeing price tables underneath all of it: the cheap tier routed to 'claude-haiku-4-5' while the billing table held only the dated identifier, so every cheap call was priced at zero and a tournament generating eighty concepts recorded CA$0.00 against a CA$25 ceiling cheap work could never reach; and routing restated the deep tier at USD 5/25 per million tokens while the provider billed 15/75, making every estimate in the system a third of the truth -- the first expedition was estimated at CA$0.15 a field and cost CA$1.02. There is one price table now, routing reads it rather than restating it, and an unpriced model is refused at construction instead of billing zero, which is what _cost_for already said and the constructor silently disagreed with. The last model spend reaching the ledger with a null job was the model probe, which now carries the job that ran it -- an unattributed row is indistinguishable from a cost nobody caused. And the requirement asks for agent and API *minutes* as well as dollars: the gateway already measured the latency of every response and simply did not keep it, so the minutes half had no query behind it. It is persisted with the cost now and reported per artefact, because minutes says whether a thing is slow as well as expensive and those are not the same complaint. Hosting stays unattributed on purpose: it is an operating cost no single artefact caused, and spreading it to make the attribution look complete would make every unit cost wrong in the same direction, which is worse than a number saying it does not know. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: contribution per operating dollar is reported and is zero, which is the true state -- optimising it needs revenue, and no credential grants that. /api/finance.
title: Cost-to-Create and Profitable Throughput

body: After the current Claude build reaches a coherent checkpoint, send this newest upgrade file and say: Audit these upgrades against what you actually built. Merge every compatible improvement into the canonical architecture and Master Plan as v1.3. Do not rebuild working systems unnecessarily. Implement the highest-leverage missing pieces, add acceptance tests, update BUILD_STATE, and continue autonomous execution. The commercial priority is maximizing the probability of a sustainable CA$3,000/month while preserving pattern quality, platform safety and positive contribution economics. Do not stop for routine decisions. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.1 — 365-Day Seasonal Revenue Engine
note: merge instruction; this audit is its execution
title: Merge Instruction for Claude

body: Seasonal Revenue Engine Christmas remains the immediate campaign because the current September 2026 making window is open, but Brambleloop is not a Christmas business. The system must continuously operate an evergreen base plus rolling seasonal waves plus trend opportunities plus breakout amplification. Three simultaneous planning horizons: NOW / MONETIZE — products customers are actively searching for; NEXT / BUILD — events whose shopping/making windows open soon; LATER / RESEARCH — events that need product engineering, indexing and audience-building months in advance. Seasonal universe: Christmas and winter; Valentine's Day; Easter; Mother's Day; Father's Day; weddings; baby showers; births/nursery; graduation; teacher gifts; spring/garden; summer/cottage; Canada Day; July 4 where commercially relevant; back-to-school; fall/autumn; Halloween; Canadian Thanksgiving; U.S. Thanksgiving; birthdays; housewarming; and other evidence-backed occasions. Opportunity allocation: do not give every event equal resources. Score expected demand × achievable visibility × contribution potential × time remaining × product fit × competitive weakness × production feasibility. Allocate creative, engineering and growth capacity dynamically from those scores. Making-date intelligence: each event stores design deadline, engineering deadline, physical-test deadline where required, publication/indexing date, expected search-growth window, peak purchase period and practical last-making date. The system should never discover Valentine's demand on February 1 or Christmas demand in December and call that timely. Dynamic seasonal squads: the Seasonal Revenue Director may spin up temporary Christmas, Halloween, Valentine's, Easter, Mother's Day, Fall/Thanksgiving, Summer/Patriotic, Wedding/Baby and other squads when forecasted opportunity warrants them. Squads deactivate when their marginal opportunity falls below alternatives; they are not permanent token-burning agents. Evergreen floor: seasonal campaigns may receive aggressive temporary allocation, but evergreen production never drops to zero. Maintain products in durable categories such as baby, animals/amigurumi, blankets, accessories, garments, bags, gifts and home decor to smooth revenue between peaks. Cross-season reuse without cloning: validated construction primitives, production tooling and commercial lessons may be reused across seasons, but creative expression must remain original. A successful Halloween product may teach Brambleloop that low-sew mini amigurumi converts; that insight can inform Christmas or Valentine's concepts without simply recolouring the same protected design. Seasonal portfolio dashboard: show each event's days to making-window open/close, active SKU count, candidate concepts, qualified traffic, conversion, revenue, contribution, inventory of release-ready products, content readiness and current capacity allocation. Breakout Product Emergency Mode: if a seasonal or evergreen SKU materially exceeds its category/shop velocity baseline, temporarily override normal production allocation. CEO, Growth, Pricing, Content and Collection agents investigate why it is breaking out, expand legitimate distribution, create high-confidence adjacent experiments and bundles, and protect quality. QA gates remain non-bypassable. Exit emergency mode when marginal opportunity normalizes. Immediate 2026 application: Christmas should receive urgent attention now because the making window is active, while the NEXT and LATER horizons simultaneously prepare winter/Valentine's and subsequent spring/Easter/Mother's Day opportunities. The exact allocation must come from current market evidence, not a fixed percentage. Merge instruction: when this queued upgrade package is given to Claude, replace any architecture that treats 'Christmas Strike Team' as the permanent seasonal strategy with this 365-Day Seasonal Revenue Engine. Preserve Christmas as the current campaign, not the company identity. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.3.2 — Adversarial Commercial + Policy Audit These upgrades extend v1.3.1. They were added after another adversarial audit focused on Etsy policy freshness, evidence quality, autonomous-agent thrashing, customer lifecycle, financial discipline and business continuity.
note: radar/market.py has shopping-vs-making window arithmetic and dated events; no 365-day engine, horizons, squads or seasonal dashboard
title: Replace the narrow Christmas Strike Team with a permanent 365-Day

body: Any agent that observes three materially identical states without progress must stop polling and re-plan. Repeated identical tool call + identical result triggers a circuit breaker. Polling backs off exponentially. Deployment retries require a changed hypothesis/root-cause fix. Track progress-per-dollar and progress-per-iteration; suspend loops consuming budget without state change.
note: swarm/orchestrate.ThrashDetector stops on three identical call-and-result pairs and forces a re-plan. The check is on call AND result: a poll whose answer keeps changing is progress, one whose answer never does is a loop that has stopped working and started spending.
title: Stagnation / Thrash Detection

body: Before every Etsy release, classify the product under current Etsy Creativity Standards and generate required disclosures. Etsy permits seller-designed digital downloads and seller-prompted AI creations, but AI use must be disclosed where required. Policy Agent must re-fetch current policy before enabling new asset/product classes. Never assume an AI-generated lifestyle image satisfies Etsy's listing-image requirements.
note: gates/platform_policy.py classifies the product, generates the disclosures it owes, and refuses a generated image in a role that makes a claim about the finished object -- labelling it does not convert it. check_new_class() refuses a new class against an unread policy
title: Etsy Creativity / AI Disclosure Gate

body: Separate product proof from promotional concept imagery. For patterns, prioritize real tester/customer finished-project photography as soon as available. Store provenance, consent/license, pattern version, yarn/colour and whether image is physical, simulated or AI-assisted. If current Etsy policy requires seller-owned photos/video or restricts renderings for the relevant listing class, the Policy Gate blocks incompatible assets.
note: commerce/buyer_trust.record_image() stores kind, physical-vs-simulated nature, pattern version, yarn, colourway and a recorded consent basis; third-party imagery without one is refused, and gallery_proof() reports a render-only gallery as honest and not proof
title: Evidence-Backed Listing Imagery Policy

body: Marketplace Insights becomes a scarce first-party research resource. Allocate keyword queries using expected information gain: validate the highest-uncertainty/highest-value micro-markets first. Store every query/result snapshot so the same keyword is not wastefully re-queried. Etsy Plus/unlimited access is an owner-approved upgrade only when expected value exceeds cost.
note: the query budgeter allocates a resource this system still cannot query: Marketplace Insights has no endpoint among the nine this application is authorised for. Re-gated to browser_vision on 2026-09-19 for the same reason as #1. The budgeting arithmetic is buildable before the source exists and is tracked as owed rather than as blocked work.
title: Marketplace Insights Query Budgeter

body: Every trend/search datum stores source, date range, geography/population and freshness. Etsy trend reports can be based on specific populations/time windows, so agents may not present U.S.-only or historical trend data as current Canadian/global demand. Opportunity scores discount stale or mismatched evidence.
note: radar/provenance.py refuses a datum with no population or window, discounts a neighbouring population rather than dismissing it, measures staleness against the topic's own seasonality, and refuses to present a foreign or expired figure as current Canadian demand
title: Trend Data Provenance and Geography

body: Policy Agent performs scheduled checks of Etsy Seller Policy, Creativity Standards, listing-image rules, advertising rules and shilling/review rules. Material policy changes create a blocking incident for affected workflows until reviewed/tested. Store policy version/date with each release certificate.
note: the five policy surfaces are watched separately, a material change is a digest difference rather than a judgement, a stale or unread source opens one blocking incident, and the release certificate carries the policy stamp. Retrieval is externally blocked, verified 2026-09-19: a plain HTTPS GET of https://www.etsy.com/legal/sellers/ returns 403 from Etsy's bot protection (robots.txt fetches fine, so it is the edge refusing an automated client, not a network fault). Spoofing a browser user-agent to get past it is evasion and was not done. A legitimate retrieval path needs a real browser worker, so this is gated on browser_vision rather than left as a partial nobody is working on.
title: Policy Freshness Watch

body: Each Brambleloop pattern must carry explicit customer-use terms chosen deliberately: what the buyer may do with the PDF, whether finished physical items may be sold, redistribution prohibition, and support/version policy. The terms must be consistent across PDF, listing and FAQ and should be legally reviewed before relying on them as enforceable.
note: commerce/terms.py decides all five axes from closed options, renders the PDF, listing and FAQ from one decision, and refuses a set where the three surfaces diverge. `enforceable` stays False until a legal review is recorded
title: Product Rights / Commercial-Use Terms

body: Design digital-product messaging to prevent mistaken purchases: prominent 'DIGITAL CROCHET PATTERN — NOT A FINISHED ITEM', skill level, required materials, terminology and download/support instructions. Track confusion-driven contacts/refunds as a conversion-quality defect. Customer Experience prioritizes resolution before Etsy's case window where applicable.
note: six closed purchase-protecting disclosures with the digital-not-finished one required in the title, and confusion contacts counted as a listing defect rather than a cost of doing business
title: Refund / Chargeback / Case Prevention

body: Every sold product maps order -> pattern_id -> purchased version -> current safe version. When a material correction occurs, identify affected buyers and prepare policy-compliant update communication. Support always answers against the buyer's version and can explain migration to the corrected version.
note: VersionMap records order to purchased version at sale time, affected_by() names exactly which buyers a correction applies to, and correction_notice() prepares the communication without sending it
title: Pattern Version Delivery System

body: Treat physical testing as a schedulable constrained resource. Forecast upcoming Class B/C testing demand, maintain tester reliability/specialty scores, avoid one tester becoming a bottleneck, and schedule seasonal products early enough that physical QA does not miss the making window.
note: quality/testers.py forecasts testing demand from the seasonal calendar rather than the request queue, scores reliability as completed against accepted, flags a specialty resting on one tester, and refuses an assignment outside a specialty
title: Tester Capacity Marketplace

body: The recurring fictional model is one brand asset, not the brand itself. Build recognizable Brambleloop signatures: editorial layout, naming architecture, photography language, chart style, tutorial voice, collection families, customer-support experience and distinctive original design grammar. The shop must remain recognizable even on product-first listings without the model.
note: brand/moat.py inventories ten signatures with how long each would take a competitor, separates built from planned, and shows the brand surviving the loss of the canonical model on two structural advantages
title: Brand Moat Beyond the Model

body: When adding adjacent products and bundles, measure whether they create incremental revenue or merely move buyers from a higher-contribution SKU. Attribute bundle uplift, attach rate and cannibalization before declaring Winner Amplification successful.
note: commerce/attribution.py measures attach rate, incrementality and cannibalisation against a pre-bundle baseline, and amplification_check() refuses to declare a winner on revenue: contribution decides
title: Product Cannibalization / Bundle Attribution

body: Pricing experiments build a category-specific elasticity history. Record price, sale state, traffic source, season, conversion, AOV and contribution. Avoid interpreting seasonal traffic changes as price effects. Use genuine regular prices and truthful temporary promotions.
note: commerce/elasticity.py records price points with season, traffic source and sale state as columns, and refuses a comparison across any of them. An unmeasured elasticity is reported as unmeasured, never as zero
title: Price Elasticity Memory

body: For new products with no sales, diagnose sequentially: insufficient impressions -> query/distribution; impressions/no clicks -> thumbnail/title; clicks/no favourites/cart -> product appeal; favourites/cart/no purchase -> price/trust/offer; purchases/refunds/support -> product quality. Do not retire a product before enough exposure exists to identify the stage failing.
note: growth/portfolio.classify runs all five of #47's stages; the APPEAL_PROBLEM rung distinguishes clicks that produced no saves (the product) from saves that produced no orders (the offer), and NO_EVIDENCE blocks retirement before there is exposure to diagnose
title: Zero-Sale Diagnostic Ladder

body: Where practical, maintain small organic/control cohorts before scaling paid promotion so the system can distinguish genuine listing/product improvement from traffic purchased by ads. Record assisted versus direct outcomes.
note: commerce/elasticity.holdout() measures incremental orders against what the organic control predicts for the promoted arm's traffic, and refuses to separate anything with only one arm
title: Launch Cohort Holdout

body: Revenue does not automatically become ad budget. Define a cash reserve, tax reserve, operating reserve and reinvestment envelope. CFO can recommend reinvestment based on marginal contribution and confidence, but consequential increases remain owner-gated.
note: finance/reinvestment.py fills tax, operating and cash reserves in order; the envelope is what survives them, scaled by the modelled confidence, and no code path returns owner_approval_required False
title: Cash-to-Growth Reinvestment Policy

body: Continuously map dependencies: Etsy account, Railway, Postgres, model providers, GitHub, domain/email, payment rails, tester network and key traffic channels. Each critical dependency gets backup/export/recovery strategy proportional to business impact.
note: ops/dependencies.py maps nine dependencies graded by what stops rather than by vendor, refuses one with no recovery strategy, probes configuration where it can and reports None where it cannot
title: Single-Point Dependency Map

body: Nightly or scheduled exports preserve CIRs, PDFs, charts, listing copy/assets metadata, customer-support knowledge, competitor snapshots, experiments and financial ledger in portable formats. The company must be reconstructable if a SaaS provider disappears.
