body: Each agent/cell maintains a versioned capability profile: objective, baseline metrics, mistakes, lessons, successful tactics, rejected tactics, current prompt/policy/tool versions and challenger experiments. Agents regularly review their own outcomes and propose evidence-backed improvements.
note: improve/profiles.py assembles each cell's versioned capability profile from the rows rather than storing a second copy beside them: objective, metric and how it is measured, baseline and latest, promoted/rejected/reverted tactics, lessons in reach, running config versions and their challengers. A cell never measured has no capability rather than a capability of zero. self_review() proposes only from patterns in that cell's own record -- a run of three measurements the wrong way (a run is a direction, a point is weather), a metric never measured or stale past 30 days, a tactic family rejected twice for the same reason, a lesson routed here and never acted on -- and each proposal carries the rows it came from. Deterministic on purpose: a cell that writes fluent hypotheses every week looks exactly like a cell that is learning. A clean record proposes nothing and says so. Nothing here promotes: proposals enter the ordinary pipeline with its governance check, sandbox result and risk tier. /api/profiles.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Every Agent Has a Learning Loop

body: Learning may occur continuously as evidence arrives; promotion of changes follows controlled cadence and risk tier. Low-risk scoring/prompt improvements may be tested frequently. Code, release logic, spend, policy and truth gates require regression/adversarial testing and rollback. Never equate 'constant learning' with uncontrolled production mutation.
note: improve/tiers.py grades every self-change by what it touches, never by what it is called -- a spend limit adjusted inside a change described as a scoring tweak is still a spend change, and the description is the part somebody chooses. Five tiers from scoring to gate, each with a cooldown (six changes to one surface in an afternoon cannot be attributed to anything), a rolling weekly ceiling (continuous learning with no ceiling is a company rewriting itself faster than it can observe the result) and the evidence its failure mode needs. An unknown surface grades upward to code, because defaulting downward would make 'touch something unlisted' the fast path. The gate tier -- truth gates, policy, release logic, spend, publication -- never promotes without an owner approval among its evidence. Enforced rather than offered: cells.promote() refuses an improvement that does not declare what it touches or that outruns its tier. /api/tiers.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: High-Frequency Learning Without Blind Self-Modification

body: Create dedicated meta-agents whose sole job is to improve other agents and departments. Include evaluator, failure-miner, experiment designer, prompt/tool challenger, cost optimizer, reliability engineer, creative critic and cross-department lesson router. Their work is measured by verified uplift, not number of changes.
note: improve/roles.py names the eight meta-agents the requirement lists and enforces the three rules that stop such a swarm flattering itself. The requirement's own last clause is the danger and is implemented as arithmetic rather than as a policy: scorecard() computes from realised uplift alone and proposals_made cannot reach the score, because a swarm graded on changes made will make changes -- forty findings, thirty proposals, twelve promotions, and no capability curve that moved. A rejected proposal scores zero and never negative, since penalising rejection teaches the swarm to propose only what will obviously pass, and a challenger that proposes only safe changes has stopped being one. No role both proposes and judges. Opposed objectives name what they may not trade: the cost optimiser may not buy savings from reliability, the reliability engineer may not buy uptime from contribution, and no role may trade deterministic validation. Remaining: the roster is a specification of roles rather than running agents -- none of the eight has an entry in agents/registry.py, a job type, a daily ceiling or a cadence, so nothing is executing these rules on a schedule yet. That is what would make this covered, and it is honest to say it has not been done rather than to count the definitions.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Improvement Swarm

body: For important functions, maintain incumbent and challenger configurations. Replay representative historical tasks plus fresh holdouts, compare quality/cost/latency/reliability, and promote only statistically/operationally meaningful improvements. Preserve rollback and prevent test-set overfitting.
note: improve/league.py was built for #95/#96 and already held most of this: incumbent and challenger configurations, a fixed shared task set, a refusal of any challenger judged on tasks it introduced, cost and reliability as outcomes rather than footnotes, and the reason for every version recorded. #180 added the four things it was quietly missing. Latency is now the fourth axis, and it is the one that looks free because it is nobody's line item until a cadence misses its window. required_margin() scales the promotion bar by how many tasks were measured, because QUALITY_MARGIN on four tasks is a coin and a league promoting on coins churns while every report counting promotions calls it progress. A holdout is carried alongside the shared set and never tuned against -- refusing self-introduced tasks stops one author gaming one comparison and does nothing about the slower version, where a hundred challengers judged over a year against the same forty tasks are selected for those forty and nobody ever brought a task of their own; winning the tuned set while losing the holdout is the signature, and a holdout overlapping the shared set is refused as the same evidence twice. rollback() restores a named previous version with a required reason, and rollback_target() answers what would be restored before anybody needs it, because the moment a rollback is needed is the moment nobody can reconstruct what was running last Tuesday. A comparison with no holdout is reported as tuned_set_only rather than refused: it is a weaker claim, not an invalid one.

title: Agent Challenger League

A local machine may be used for optional development, heavy one-off rendering, manual review or emergency recovery, but the production control plane and durable state must remain cloud-hosted. body: A public website is not required merely to keep agents alive. The runtime needs a secure owner operations console/dashboard accessible from phone/desktop showing health, queues, products, agent activity, spend, incidents, approvals, experiments, deployment version and learning changes. This may live in the existing cloud app; do not build a public marketing site unless it has a separate business case.
note: /api/console is the single request an absent owner makes, assembling what the requirement names -- health, queues, products, agent activity, spend, incidents, approvals, experiments, deployment version and learning changes -- from the endpoints that already serve each. The two gaps this requirement was carrying are closed: approvals arrive as the executor's own cards, each with its action and its consequence of waiting, because a count of queued actions does not answer 'is anything waiting on me'; and learning changes arrive from the observation record with their source and date. Both are also on the dashboard page itself, so the answer is readable on a phone without composing a request. Health is #185's verdict rather than a liveness ping, which means the console can say `idle` -- a console that cannot say so is one that will report a green week of nothing. Every dashboard block is individually guarded: a page that fails to render because one subsystem is unhappy tells the owner nothing about the twelve that are fine. On exposure: the console aggregates what the individual read endpoints already serve at the same exposure and opens no new door; the two write paths, the continuity export and the dead-letter requeue, stay behind the operator credential. No public marketing site exists or is planned, which is the requirement's other half.

title: Website Is Optional; Operations Console Is Required

body: All recurring work uses durable cloud scheduling and leased/idempotent queues. Restarts, deploys and transient failures must not lose jobs or duplicate commercial actions. Test kill/restart/reclaim, clock drift, overlapping schedules, dead-letter recovery and exactly-once-effect behavior for sensitive actions.
note: queue/durable.py leases with idempotency keys and dead letters; test_persistence.py SIGKILLs a worker and proves recovery
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Durable Scheduler + Queue Guarantees

body: Continuously monitor worker heartbeat, scheduler freshness, queue age, DB health, external integrations, browser/vision workers, model gateways, certificate freshness and spend. Automatically restart/requeue within authority, escalate persistent incidents, and preserve evidence. 'Online' means useful work is progressing, not merely that HTTP returns 200.
note: ops/health.py takes the requirement's own definition literally: online means useful work is progressing, not that HTTP returned 200. A container can serve 200s, tick a worker, run a scheduler, hold an empty queue and complete nothing for a week, with every liveness signal green, because none of them is about work -- this build's recurring defect in its most respectable costume, a verdict computed from the absence of failures on a system that is doing nothing and therefore has none. So `progress` (jobs completed in a six-hour window) is a signal with the same standing as the heartbeat, and an otherwise-green system reports `idle` rather than `healthy`; the two are different words on purpose. Queue age is the companion: a live worker and a job pending for three hours is a worker that is alive and not working, which reads as healthy on any dashboard that counts processes. All nine signals the requirement names are read, a deliberate refusal in the dead-letter queue is counted apart from a defect -- found by reading the live console rather than a test, because production holds 134 dead letters and every one is a publication refused by shadow mode, so reporting them as a repair backlog would put a permanent false number on the page and a number that is always there is a number nobody reads -- and an unconfigured integration is `unknown` rather than down, because reporting a gate as a fault makes the dashboard red for a decision nobody has made. Writing the self-healing half produced the finding that replaced it: both obvious repairs already exist. A lease is reclaimed inside JobQueue.claim on every claim, and a dead letter is re-driven once per deploy (B-327), which is the right trigger -- a dead letter is fixed by a code change, so a fifteen-minute timer would re-run a failure nothing has fixed ninety-six times a day, which is a retry storm with a health check's name on it. The module therefore detects, escalates and names where each repair actually lives, and what it cannot fix at all -- a container restart, a missing credential, money already spent -- it escalates by name rather than attempting, because a repair that is announced and does not happen is worse than none: nobody looks. Escalation waits for persistence: one bad sweep is a blip and a deploy produces several, so an incident is raised only after three consecutive sweeps, carrying the readings that produced it, and the history is read from the handler's own audit trail rather than memory because a container replacement is exactly when conditions happen. Two signals are read from the present moment rather than from a shared variable: this sweep executing at all proves a worker is alive, and the job arriving from a cadence proves the scheduler ticked. runner.STATE is process-local, so in a split deployment the process reading it is not the one writing it and the heartbeat would read None forever -- an hourly 'the worker is down' raised by a worker that is demonstrably running, which is exactly the noise this module refuses elsewhere. Cadence: health_sweep -> ops.health every fifteen minutes. /api/health-signals.

title: 24/7 Health and Self-Healing

body: When no urgent queue exists, agents should not sit idle merely to satisfy a 24/7 slogan. They should consume a prioritized backlog: market research, competitor change detection, creative tournaments, benchmark analysis, catalogue QA, SEO experiments, learning replays, documentation, cost optimization and improvement experiments. Avoid pointless token-burning loops.
note: an idle agent takes the highest-value standing backlog item rather than polling to look alive, which spends money to produce a heartbeat, or stopping, which makes the 24/7 claim false.

title: Work-Conserving Autonomy

body: Allocate autonomous capacity by expected business value and deadlines: customer incidents and truth defects first; imminent seasonal windows next; proven high-value product opportunities; listing/creative bottlenecks; experiments; background research. Prevent 500 low-value agents from starving one critical release.
note: eight priority bands, and a band is never traded away for value: a CA$5,000 opportunity with a one-day deadline does not outrank a customer incident. Deadline and value decide within a band only.
section: 24/7 cloud autonomy, agent swarms, continuous learning
title: Priority Scheduler

body: Large swarms require centralized budget control. Track cost per agent, task, product, department and experiment; enforce daily/monthly ceilings, anomaly detection and marginal-value thresholds. Scale parallelism up when it materially improves throughput/quality and down when it only duplicates work.
note: finance/governor.py is the view across the ceilings that already refuse. Cost is attributed across the five dimensions the requirement names -- agent, task, product, department, experiment -- and every dollar is either attributed or named unattributed, with the two summing to the bill or the table being refused outright. That reconciliation is the point: an attribution table that sums to less than the invoice is the commonest finance artefact in a company this size and is worse than none, because it is acted on, and the missing spend is always the spend nobody has a story for. Three of the requirement's four controls are measurements this company cannot take yet, and the module's value is refusing to fake them. An anomaly needs a baseline: below fourteen days of history it reports that it cannot say, because a detector with no baseline fires on the first real day of work, teaches everybody to ignore it, and then never fires again -- and a dollar floor sits under the statistical threshold, since on a base of pennies every multiple is a spike. Marginal value has a zero numerator while no order has been attributed to any spend, and reporting that as 'every spend is worthless' is arithmetic rather than a finding: it would justify cutting the spend that has not had time to work, so it is reported as unmeasurable, naming what it needs. Parallelism cannot be judged from one setting of it -- the question is whether adding a worker changed anything, and a single number answers with whatever was running when somebody asked -- so advise refuses below two distinct worker counts, and judges on completions per *minute* rather than per worker-minute, because the latter always falls when a worker is added and the question is whether the queue drained faster. A second worker that moved throughput less than 10% took turns on dependent work and is cost without throughput. The live control remains the daily and lifetime ceilings, which refuse before a spend rather than reporting after it. /api/governor.

note: visual/identity.py holds candidates and exactly one canonical slot, and nothing moves between them without the owner. select() refuses without approval, refuses an incomplete reference pack, and refuses to replace an existing canonical identity -- approving a selection is not approving a redesign. Remaining: no candidate has been generated, because that needs the image capability.
title: Permanent Identity Lock

body: Every model-led asset must pass identity-consistency checks against the canonical reference pack. A beautiful image of the wrong woman fails. Detect gradual face drift, hair/eye drift, age drift and stylization drift across batches and over time. Failed assets regenerate before release.
note: drift_check compares against the reference pack across face, hair, eyes, age and stylisation, and an unmeasured dimension counts as maximum drift rather than being skipped. With no pack the verdict is 'unavailable' and blocks release -- never 'pass'. A check that passed for want of a reference would be believed. Remaining: the pack itself.
title: Model Anti-Drift Release Gate

body: The canonical model is attractive and premium but appropriately dressed for the product, season and Etsy shopping context. Garments must remain the commercial subject. Styling should resemble high-end crochet/lifestyle editorial photography, not glamour imagery that distracts from fit, texture, construction or product details.
note: canonical model: needs an image-generation capability and owner identity selection
title: Appropriate Product-First Styling

body: For model-appropriate products, generate a coherent shot plan: primary product-first hero, full/three-quarter fit, front/back/side as relevant, texture/detail, sleeve/neckline/closure/construction detail, scale/context and optional lifestyle shot. The model must increase trust, aspiration and brand recognition while preserving truthful product representation.
note: shot_plan() produces a job per frame -- hero, fit, detail, scale, construction, evidence -- rather than a target count, because #80 asks for minimum quality and a count produces filler.
title: Model Merchandising Shot System

body: Use the same canonical fictional model across appropriate clothing, accessories, seasonal holding/presentation shots and brand/editorial content so customers develop recognition. Do not force her into product categories where a clean product-only hero is commercially stronger. Product truth and category fit outrank compulsory model presence.
note: twelve product forms are product-first, and the model is not forced into them: a clean product-only hero is commercially stronger for a blanket, and product truth outranks compulsory brand recognition.
title: Model Identity Across the Store

body: Maintain a canonical registry of elite crochet-market benchmarks rather than relying on vague memory. Each benchmark records canonical URL, shop identity, categories, reason for inclusion, scan health, last baseline, last change, evidence freshness and specialist cells responsible. MJsOffTheHookDesigns is a mandatory anchor benchmark because the owner selected it as the primary quality/commercial reference.
note: intel/benchmarks.py declares the registry and core/models.Benchmark stores its observed state -- canonical URL, owner-supplied URL, mandate, categories, responsible pods, scan health and the three freshness timestamps. Seeded at boot and reconciled like the agent registry: code owns identity, the running system owns observed state. The panel is deliberately narrow (see #219): entries join it from evidence, never pre-populated.
title: Permanent Elite Benchmark Registry

body: Canonical benchmark URL: https://www.etsy.com/ca/shop/MJsOffTheHookDesigns . Store this literal reference in configuration and documentation. Validate URL health and resolution; if Etsy changes routing, resolve the shop's current canonical location without silently substituting a different seller.
note: the canonical URL is a literal in intel/benchmarks.py and in the registry table. resolve() validates health through an injected fetcher and classifies the result healthy / moved / unreachable / wrong_shop / unverified. A redirect that lands on a different seller, or on a search page, is refused and never re-points the registry -- record_resolution() follows a move and ignores a wrong_shop. No capability configured reports unverified, never healthy.
title: Mandatory MJsOffTheHookDesigns Source

body: On first successful browser/vision integration, enumerate the complete discoverable MJsOffTheHookDesigns catalogue rather than sampling only top listings. Record listing identity, category, visible pricing/sale state, merchandising format, media count/types, product family and dated evidence. Coverage gaps must be explicit.
note: intel/observe.py enumerates the complete catalogue by pagination rather than sampling, records listing identity, category, price, sale state, media count, product family and dated evidence, and marks the first pass as a baseline. Remaining: it has never run against Etsy, because the credential does not exist; every branch is exercised against an injected reader instead.
title: MJs Full-Catalogue Baseline

body: Every discoverable benchmark listing selected for baseline/deep audit is individually opened. Capture and analyze all accessible listing gallery assets, video where accessible, title, visible description, price/sale presentation, options/variants, badges, product claims, digital-delivery positioning, cross-sell cues and other commercially relevant listing structure. Do not claim an audit occurred if only search-result thumbnails were seen.
note: the deep audit opens each new or changed listing individually and traverses its gallery, capturing title, description, price, tags, materials, favourites and per-image colour statistics. It never claims an audit from a catalogue row: audit_state only becomes 'audited' after the gallery call succeeded. Remaining: video, variants and badges, and the fact that nothing has been run against Etsy.
title: Listing-by-Listing Deep Audit

body: Browser agents must inspect the actual gallery, not merely scrape text. For every accessible image, derive non-copying commercial observations: shot type, composition, product visibility, model/product relationship, setting, scale communication, detail coverage, infographic use, typography, palette role, thumbnail readability and emotional merchandising. Preserve dated evidence/provenance.
note: every audited gallery becomes pending analysis work with a stable per-image identity, ordered newest-first because that is the order commercial value arrives in; intel/vision.py reports the backlog size and what it would cost. The observation vocabulary is closed. Remaining: no image has been judged, because no model provider is configured -- and record() refuses an observation produced without looking at the image.
title: Vision-Level Gallery Analysis

body: Create independent specialist cells for the major product departments observed in the benchmark catalogue: garments/clothing, blankets/throws, stockings, ornaments/tree decor, home/decor, bags/accessories, hats/wearables, seasonal/gift products and additional categories as discovered. Each cell owns category-specific history, quality rubric, opportunity map and competitive lessons.
note: intel/pods.py defines the eight mandated specialist cells with ordered routing and a per-pod quality rubric, and BenchmarkObservation carries per-pod evidence. Remaining: each pod's opportunity map and category history are structurally present but empty until observation exists, and pod-level learning memory is #226/#177-194 work.
title: MJs Specialist Intelligence Pods

body: A central director coordinates specialist pods, deduplicates observations, identifies cross-category mechanisms, routes new benchmark releases to the correct cells, and prevents siloed learning. It maintains a company-level view of where Brambleloop is ahead, at parity or materially behind on concrete dimensions without using that as permission to copy protected expression.
note: intel/pods.Director deduplicates on content fingerprint, routes listings to the answering pod, finds mechanisms appearing across two or more pods, and computes ahead/parity/behind per concrete dimension -- with unknown, never parity, when either side has no evidence. Remaining: the company-level view is computed on demand rather than maintained, and has no evidence to compute from yet.
title: Central Competitive Intelligence Director

body: Do not wastefully re-download/reason over an unchanged full catalogue every 30 minutes. First establish complete baseline coverage. Thereafter run lightweight change detection frequently and trigger immediate deep audits for newly discovered listings or materially changed listings/assets. Periodically re-baseline to detect missed changes.
note: baseline, fingerprint-based change detection, and reconciliation: a listing that vanishes is marked withdrawn and kept, never deleted -- 'we saw this for six weeks and then it stopped' is a finding, an absent row is indistinguishable from a listing that never existed. Announced once, not on every later scan.
title: Baseline Then Change Detection

body: Monitoring frequency adapts to observed posting/change behaviour, seasonal urgency and evidence freshness. During active release periods or major seasonal ramps, checks may be frequent; during quiet periods they back off. The objective is near-immediate discovery of commercially meaningful changes without pointless compute burn.
note: intel/cadence.py adapts the interval from recorded change rate, consecutive quiet scans and seasonal proximity, moving one step at a time so it cannot oscillate. Deliberately asymmetric: a busy shop speeds it up immediately, a quiet one only after four consecutive empty scans, because being too slow during a release run misses the event the mission exists to catch while being too fast costs calls the fingerprint already makes nearly free. History is read from recorded scans, so a restart does not reset it.
title: Adaptive Monitoring Cadence

body: A new MJs listing becomes a structured market event. Archive dated observations, classify category, notify relevant specialist pods, decompose the commercial mechanisms, update category benchmark standards, run opportunity analysis and decide whether it justifies an original Brambleloop concept tournament.
note: a new listing becomes a structured event: archived with dated evidence, classified into a pod, routed, and turned into queued work through the coverage gap queue. Remaining: mechanism decomposition and the concept tournament it should trigger.
title: New-Listing Event Pipeline

body: Brambleloop is allowed to enter the same broad/generic product arena when market evidence supports it - e.g., cardigan, stocking, blanket, hat, ornament or coaster. Agents should identify what makes the benchmark compelling and design a substantively original Brambleloop alternative with stronger product engineering, styling, usability, fit, construction, creativity or customer experience. Do not restrict Brambleloop merely because an elite competitor also sells that generic product type.
note: same-arena response lane, breakthrough response lane
title: Same-Arena Response Lane

body: In parallel, benchmark releases should trigger a more divergent tournament asking what the competitor has NOT made: adjacent functions, new recipients, transformations, silhouettes, construction systems, bundles, seasonal stories and collection families. Maintain both incremental market participation and breakthrough exploration.
note: creative/breakthrough.py runs the divergent lane across the eight axes the requirement names, drawing each axis's vocabulary from the closed lists and excluding what the catalogue already covers. The load-bearing part is the label: 'what the competitor has NOT made' is a claim about their catalogue and requires having looked, so with nothing observed the divergence runs against our own catalogue and every brief says so. check_claim() refuses a brief that describes itself as an unserved market gap on that basis -- the thing nobody has made and the thing we happen not to have made are different discoveries, and only one is an opportunity. Both lanes are held open by a floor: incremental work has a visible customer and breakthrough work has an argument, so the argument loses every planning round unless something stops it. /api/breakthrough.
title: Breakthrough Response Lane

body: Store reusable lessons only at the mechanism level: silhouette strength, fit strategy, styling, colour architecture, photography coverage, product family logic, beginner support, seasonal timing, thumbnail clarity, merchandising, bundle logic and customer promise. Do not turn competitor protected pattern text/images into Brambleloop source designs.
note: lessons are stored only against a closed mechanism vocabulary, and pods.lesson() refuses a note carrying a competitor's row-by-row instructions, chart or pattern text. The refusal is at the point of writing rather than at a review nobody schedules.
title: Benchmark Mechanism Decomposition

body: For relevant categories, place Brambleloop candidates beside current category-matched MJs benchmark evidence in a blinded comparison. Evaluate concept desirability, distinctiveness, product clarity, thumbnail strength, styling, apparent craftsmanship, giftability and purchase confidence. If Brambleloop looks obviously generic/amateur by comparison, return it to creative development rather than shipping.
note: MJs challenge gate; needs MJs evidence
title: MJs Challenge Gate

body: MJs is the anchor, not the only teacher. Maintain a changing elite panel including other category leaders and purchased Benchmark Library products. A category specialist should learn from the best available examples across sellers so Brambleloop can combine best-of-breed mechanisms and avoid overfitting to one shop's aesthetic.
note: elite panel beyond one seller
title: Elite Panel Beyond One Seller

body: When MJs or another elite benchmark materially improves presentation, product format or customer experience, relevant Brambleloop standards are re-evaluated. The competitive bar is dynamic. Improvement Department records which standards changed and why.
note: benchmark quality bar moves
title: Benchmark Quality Bar Moves

body: The MJs/elite benchmark observation layer requires production-capable browser traversal plus image/gallery understanding that operates in cloud infrastructure with owner devices off. Build 2 must not silently replace this with static seeded data, occasional manual screenshots or text-only search. Missing capability is an explicit owner/integration gate.
note: the cloud browser/vision capability is the thing being requested, so it cannot be built without it; parked on the browser_vision gate rather than counted as executable
title: Mandatory Cloud Browser + Vision Capability

body: Prove end-to-end capability against the canonical benchmark: resolve shop URL; enumerate catalogue; open multiple listings; traverse gallery assets; capture visible listing text/commerce metadata; produce image-level observations; classify into specialist pods; persist evidence; detect a simulated/new change; and trigger a re-audit. Evidence must show each step actually occurred.
note: the browser/vision acceptance test cannot run without the capability it tests; parked on the browser_vision gate
title: Browser/Vision Acceptance Test

body: The owner has stated willingness to approve reasonable access required to implement mandatory benchmark browser/vision observation and 24/7 autonomy. Claude must present any required connection, service, credential, paid infrastructure or permission as a concise approval request with exact purpose, capability unlocked, expected/max cost, security scope and consequence of declining. Never interpret willingness as blanket authorization for unbounded spend or credentials.
note: launch/access.py states every required credential or service as a structured AccessRequest carrying exact action, purpose, capability unlocked, security scope, max cost, a monthly ceiling, minutes, consequence of declining and what continues regardless. A recurring cost without a ceiling cannot be constructed, which is the blank cheque this requirement forbids. The requests join the one consolidated owner queue through launch.readiness, keyed so a re-run restates rather than duplicates. tests/test_access.py.
title: Access Approval Protocol

body: If Etsy access, anti-bot controls, authentication, tooling limitations or other constraints prevent the mandated depth of observation, report the exact limitation and preserve the requirement as unmet. Do not claim 'continuous MJs scanning' based on search snippets or stale cached evidence.
note: access.accept_evidence() grades every piece of benchmark evidence and refuses to let a substitute close a mandate, and etsy_public.capability_report() states, per mandate element, what the sanctioned API covers and what it does not -- with a proposed compliant alternative for each gap and no gap left unaccompanied. The rendered page is recorded as unmet rather than approximated.
title: No Silent Downgrade

body: Cache content fingerprints and analysis so unchanged listings are not repeatedly paid for in model/browser compute. New images, changed descriptions, pricing/sale shifts, new video or new listing identity invalidate only the necessary analysis nodes and propagate lessons through the dependency graph.
note: gateway/routing.py caches analysis on a content fingerprint that includes the routed model, so unchanged evidence is never paid for twice and a routing change cannot silently keep serving a better model's answers. A cached answer ledgers zero cost rather than recording tokens nobody spent.
title: Competitor Evidence Cache

body: Every MJs/category pod participates in the continuous-learning architecture from #177-194: maintain category mistakes, new mechanisms, successful Brambleloop responses, failed responses, current benchmarks and challenger strategies. The pod should become measurably more discerning and creative over time.
note: specialist pod continuous learning
title: Specialist Pod Continuous Learning

body: No agent may treat 'match MJs' as the final creative objective. The benchmark establishes a commercial quality floor and a source of market evidence. Brambleloop's Creative Department must still search for original white space, new product forms and stronger customer value beyond what the benchmark currently offers.
note: competitive learning is input, not creative ceiling
title: Competitive Learning Is Input, Not Creative Ceiling

body: Until automated creative evaluation has demonstrated reliable alignment with the owner's standards, the owner retains veto over canonical model identity and flagship creative quality. Repeated veto reasons become structured training/evaluation evidence for the Improvement Department rather than disappearing as chat feedback. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.4.1 - CA$5K/Month Scale Architecture Primary commercial objective: materially increase the probability of reaching a sustainable CA$5,000/month run rate. This upgrade expands Brambleloop from product/search excellence into a diversified acquisition, offer, retention and portfolio-growth machine. A 75%+ confidence claim remains evidence-gated, not promised by architecture alone.
note: owner quality veto with structured veto memory
title: Owner Quality Veto

body: After launch validation, the commercial operating target is a sustainable CA$5,000/month gross-revenue run rate with positive contribution economics. The system must decompose this into multiple feasible combinations of qualified visits, conversion, AOV, repeat purchase and external/direct sales, then identify the binding constraint weekly.
note: scale/target.py holds the target as arithmetic rather than a slogan: seven scenarios decomposing CA$5,000 into orders, AOV, required qualified visits, repeat share and off-platform share, each carrying gross AND contribution after Etsy's transaction fee, payment processing, listing fee and refunds. binding_constraint() ranks the five numbers by share of what the balanced scenario needs, because a 400-visit gap and a 0.4-point conversion gap are not comparable as differences.
title: CA$5K/Month Becomes the Primary Commercial Scale Target

body: Do not claim >=75% modeled confidence of reaching/sustaining CA$5,000/month merely because the architecture is sophisticated. Require multiple independent selling SKUs, positive contribution, stable quality/refund/support metrics, repeatable qualified traffic, observed conversion over meaningful samples, at least two viable acquisition loops or one exceptionally strong loop with backup, and downside scenario analysis. Display assumptions and sensitivity.
note: scale/confidence.py cannot report >=75% on architecture. Every rung counts rows; observed rates are shrunk toward the pessimistic prior by sample size; everything measured from orders is bounded by the ledger's order count, so a caller cannot argue the model upward with counts from systems that do not exist yet; and the #275 gate caps the figure at 0.74 until six evidence counts are met. Today, against 15 certified patterns and zero customers, it reports 0.0 and says no amount of further building moves it.
title: 75% Confidence Is an Evidence Gate

body: Design the catalogue so CA$5K does not require one viral hit. Maintain a base of evergreen earners, seasonal earners, flagships, quick-makes, bundles and experimental shots. Track concentration: revenue share of top 1/top 5 SKUs, seasonal concentration and channel concentration. High concentration triggers diversification while preserving winner exploitation.
note: growth/portfolio.py measures role mix against a healthy range and names the roles absent entirely, and concentration reports the SKU the company depends on. An empty portfolio has undefined concentration rather than perfect diversity -- a divide-by-nothing reports perfect health for a shop with no products.
title: Revenue Portfolio Architecture

body: Assign each SKU a portfolio role: HERO traffic/revenue driver, CORE reliable evergreen/seasonal earner, ENTRY low-friction acquisition product, BUNDLE/AOV builder, CROSS-SELL attachment product, EXPERIMENT learning vehicle or RETIRE candidate. Product creation is guided by portfolio gaps rather than raw listing count.
note: seven declared roles, and an invented one is refused. Roles are declared so a gap is something the system can see, which is what lets product creation follow portfolio gaps rather than listing count.
title: Hero / Core / Long-Tail SKU Roles

body: Engineer an intentional value ladder: free/low-friction content -> entry pattern -> premium single -> mini bundle -> flagship collection -> repeat seasonal/collection purchase. Measure movement between tiers, attach rate, contribution and customer lifetime value. Avoid discounts that train customers to ignore regular pricing.
note: commerce/ladder.py engineers the ladder rather than describing it. shape() names the rungs with nothing on them -- a buyer who climbs to one arrives and finds nothing, which is not a gap in a diagram -- and the step between two occupied rungs, because a buyer who has spent CA$4 does not next spend CA$20 and a rung five times the last one is a missing step wearing a price. Free content and the repeat purchase are excluded from the gap list on purpose: one is #10's subject and the other is an outcome rather than a product somebody builds. The requirement's own sentence about discounts is made mechanical: a tier discounted on more than a third of its live days has no regular price left, because a price that is on sale that often is a higher number that appears before the real one and the buyer learns to wait. Depth and duration are commerce/promotion.py's constants, imported rather than restated; what this adds is that the damage differs by rung -- discounting the entry pattern teaches a buyer to wait, which is survivable, while the flagship collection is the one product whose job is to say what this shop is worth and no later full price recovers it. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: tier movement, attach rate, contribution and lifetime value all need a buyer. Each is reported as unmeasurable with what it needs, and lifetime_value() refuses to call a set of first purchases a lifetime value, because that is an average order value with a longer name. /api/ladder.
title: Revenue Ladder Offers

body: Continuously identify natural product combinations and test bundles/collection offers. Track bundle attach rate, incremental AOV, cannibalization and contribution. Etsy currently supports discounted bundles and targeted offers; use available mechanisms only when policy-compliant and profitable.
note: commerce/bundles.py does the half that was missing and delegates the half that exists. The measurement -- attach rate, incremental value, cannibalisation, contribution -- is commerce/attribution.py's bundle_effect, which refuses without a baseline window because the after-window alone shows a bundle selling and says nothing about where its buyers came from; a second implementation beside it would be a second answer to the same question, and in practice the more flattering one gets quoted. What this module adds is deciding which bundles are worth testing. 'Natural' is made checkable: the same occasion, the same yarn weight so one purchase of yarn serves both, a shared collection, the same recipient, or forms that furnish the same room -- facts about the products rather than judgements about the buyer -- and two products sharing fewer than two of them are not a bundle but a shelf, because a discount on things a buyer did not want is the cheapest way to make a catalogue look busy. A bundle of one pod is a set and one across four is a raffle: the coherence that makes somebody buy it is the coherence that makes it describable in a title. The price check is not margin, since at zero marginal cost a digital bundle always looks profitable -- it is whether the discount is deep enough to be a reason (10%) and shallow enough that the singles survive it, sharing promotion.py's steep-discount ceiling. Candidates are pairs, because a three-product bundle that fails tells you nothing about which pairing was wrong. /api/ladder.
title: Bundle Attach-Rate Engine

body: Where Etsy supports and the buyer is eligible/opted-in, test abandoned-cart, favorited-item, interested-shopper and thank-you offers. Measure incremental conversion, margin and repeat purchase versus baseline; do not assume every discount is accretive. Preserve truthful regular prices and promotion rules.
note: re-audited 2026-09-19. Targeted offers are seller-dashboard promotions, and the requirement's own measurement -- incremental conversion, margin and repeat purchase versus baseline, do not assume every discount is accretive -- needs orders. With zero sales there is no baseline to be incremental to, so this is data-gated rather than credential-gated, and running a promotion is separately a consequential owner action this system does not take.
title: Etsy Targeted-Offer Optimizer

body: Use Etsy Marketplace Insights as first-party demand/competition evidence once accessible. Allocate limited free queries by expected information gain; consider Etsy Plus only through owner approval if unlimited research has positive expected value. Store search count, listing count, related terms, trend direction, date and geography/context.
note: the portfolio allocator consumes Marketplace Insights evidence, which has no API surface among this application's endpoints. Re-gated to browser_vision on 2026-09-19 for the same reason as #1.
title: Marketplace Insights Portfolio Allocator

body: Connect Etsy Stats search terms and traffic sources to listing visits, orders, revenue, contribution, support/refund and repeat purchase where data permits. Keyword strategy should optimize profitable customers, not impressions alone.
note: search-term P&L, conversion cohorts, share-of-opportunity; machinery buildable, needs real stats
title: Search-Term-to-P&L; Attribution

body: Maintain conversion baselines by category, price band, traffic source, season, shop maturity and listing age. Diagnose listings against comparable cohorts. Etsy itself defines conversion as orders divided by visits and notes photos, price, reviews, titles/descriptions and policies can affect it; Brambleloop tests those factors systematically.
note: search-term P&L, conversion cohorts, share-of-opportunity; machinery buildable, needs real stats
title: Conversion Cohort Benchmarks

body: For each target micro-market, estimate available buyer demand from first-party/observed evidence, Brambleloop qualified impressions/visits, conversion and resulting revenue. Rank opportunities by expected incremental contribution from improving visibility, CTR, conversion or offer rather than by vanity rank.
note: search-term P&L, conversion cohorts, share-of-opportunity; machinery buildable, needs real stats
title: Search Share-of-Opportunity Dashboard

body: Do not make all products compete for 'crochet pattern'. Build clusters around specific intent, recipient, season, technique, object, aesthetic, skill level and use case. Etsy query matching uses titles/tags/descriptions/categories/attributes; maximize relevant coverage without keyword stuffing.
note: commerce/portfolio.py counts both of #240's failures, and they are opposites, which is the whole difficulty: a catalogue whose listings all reach for one head term has one product's worth of visibility spread across all of them, every one ranked against every other -- and fixing that by loading each listing with every term anybody might type produces the second failure, which platforms demote for. A module counting only one would push the catalogue straight into the other. Concentration is counted per facet using the vocabulary commerce/intent already holds, which is the list of clusters the requirement names. Cannibalisation is counted per pair: two listings whose stated facet values are close to identical are competing for one query rather than covering two, and the second adds no reach, it splits it. Stuffing is counted per listing, and the title and the tags are treated differently on purpose -- marketplace furniture is excluded from the tag count, because a tag set where every slot contains 'crochet' is simply how tags work, and it is deliberately not excluded from the title, because 'Crochet Pattern Crochet Blanket Crochet Throw' is the commonest form of stuffing there is and excluding furniture would make the check blind to the case it exists for. One defect was caught by its own test rather than shipped: a facet stated by a single listing reported 100% concentration and was flagged as crowded, so the least crowded facet in the catalogue was being reported as its most crowded. One listing cannot be ranked against itself, so a sole occupant is now reported as thin coverage. A facet no listing states is absent rather than diverse, because absent is not spread. /api/portfolio.
title: Query Portfolio Diversification

body: Every important launch ships with a pre-registered experiment plan: hero variants, price hypothesis, title/tag strategy, bundle/cross-sell, content/Pinterest support and success/failure thresholds. Avoid changing many variables simultaneously without recording confounders.
note: every launch ships four pre-registered experiments with hypothesis, metric, design, success and failure lines, minimum sample and stop date. An experiment with no sample floor is refused because it concludes on its first data point, and a concluded one cannot be fed more data until it says something nicer.
title: Listing Launch Experiment Pack

body: Where practical, obtain enough organic/owned traffic to estimate listing appeal before meaningful paid scaling. Ads can be used as bounded discovery, but a weak listing should not be hidden behind paid traffic. Etsy recommends allowing adequate time for Ads performance data; paid scaling decisions must respect attribution lag.
note: paid acquisition economics; needs the shop and owner-approved ad spend
title: Organic-First Proof Before Heavy Ads

body: Calculate allowable CAC from price, fees, expected refunds, discounts, repeat contribution and margin. Ads may scale only below a risk-adjusted CAC threshold with enough data. Maintain separate new-customer CAC, blended CAC and contribution after advertising.
note: paid acquisition economics; needs the shop and owner-approved ad spend
title: Paid Acquisition Allowable CAC

body: Track orders attributed to Etsy Offsite Ads separately because fee structure can materially change contribution. Use current Etsy fee/attribution rules rather than hardcoded assumptions, and incorporate any mandatory participation threshold into forecasting.
note: paid acquisition economics; needs the shop and owner-approved ad spend
title: Offsite Ads Economics Guard

body: Where Etsy's current Share & Save or successor program is available, compare economics of qualified traffic sent through eligible trackable links versus ordinary marketplace acquisition. Use only official program rules and measure net contribution after any fee benefit.
note: paid acquisition economics; needs the shop and owner-approved ad spend
title: Share-and-Save / Direct-Link Economics

body: Create an autonomous Pinterest production system around each validated product/collection: multiple genuinely distinct pins, keyword/board mapping, seasonal lead-time scheduling, landing destination, creative testing and attribution. Avoid spammy duplicate pins. Winner pins trigger more original variants and supporting content.
note: growth/pins.py carries the instruction the requirement states outright -- avoid spammy duplicate pins -- and the mechanism is not about images. Five pins that differ in crop, overlay and filter are one pin posted five times, and they are indistinguishable from five pins to any check that looks at the file. What makes two pins different is what they are about, and there are seven reasons anybody saves one: the finished object, the fabric detail a maker judges by, the work in progress, the object in a room, the gift it makes, the scale against something familiar, and the yarn itself. A set with fewer than three distinct angles is refused, a repeated angle is the same reason to save offered twice, and the four things a pin factory produces when asked for variants -- a different crop, a different overlay, a different filter, a different aspect ratio -- are named as not being pins. Amplifying a winner means another angle: producing the successful pin again with a different overlay is the same spam arriving through the door marked success, and when every angle is used the next thing is supporting content rather than another pin. The schedule comes from seasonal/calendar.py's own milestones -- listing_indexing_date at ninety days and promotional_ramp at sixty -- rather than from dates chosen here, because a second set of seasonal dates is a second answer to when the work is late, and a pin published the week before the occasion is published after the decision. /api/pins. Remaining and parked: a pin here is an angle, a destination and a date rather than a file, because image generation is a capability nobody has granted; there is no shop, site or listing for a pin to land on, so nothing is publishable; and a pin nobody has seen has no clicks to attribute, so creative testing and attribution wait on the same gate.
title: Pinterest Search Factory

body: Build owned search clusters around buyer/maker questions connected to Brambleloop categories. Each cluster maps informational intent -> useful free content/tool -> relevant paid product/collection. Measure organic qualified visits, assisted conversion, email capture where permitted and revenue contribution.
note: growth/clusters.py builds the clusters from questions makers demonstrably asked rather than from questions that sound like searches. A keyword list produced by asking a model what crocheters search for is indistinguishable from a good one until a year of writing has been spent on it, and this company already holds a list it has evidence for: the complaint themes counted from observed reviews. A complaint is an informational intent that arrived too late -- 'the stitch counts do not add up', 'I ran out of yarn', 'it did not fit' are the questions somebody would have typed a week earlier -- so every cluster is seeded from a counted theme, and a theme nobody has seen three times is one customer's bad day rather than a cluster, on intel/observe.py's own RECURRING_AT constant. Three refusals follow. A cluster with no paid destination is a blog: the requirement's chain is informational intent -> free content -> product, and the third link is the one that goes missing first because the first two are enjoyable to make, so each cluster names the product and why somebody whose question was just answered would want it -- and the download cluster says outright that it sells least of all, which is better than pretending every article sells something. Two clusters answering the same question in the same department rank against each other, which is #240's catalogue cannibalisation wearing a different hat: the fix for a thin cluster is depth and the instinct is a second article. The free kinds are growth/free_to_paid.py's, imported rather than restated. Clusters are ranked by how often the question was actually asked, which is a measurement rather than a guess. /api/clusters. Remaining and parked: organic qualified visits, assisted conversion, email capture and revenue contribution all need a site with organic traffic, and reporting them as zeroes would make an unbuilt funnel look like a failed one.
title: Google / SEO Topic Cluster Engine

body: Flagships and technique-heavy products generate reusable video modules: product reveal, technique explanation, progress checkpoints, troubleshooting and finished-result clips. Repurpose appropriately across YouTube/Shorts/Pinterest/social while keeping a canonical tutorial. Track assisted conversion and support reduction.
note: growth/video.py carries the five modules the requirement names and the instruction with real weight in it: keeping a canonical tutorial. The reason is not tidiness. Five platform videos with no canonical source diverge silently -- the pattern is corrected, the written instructions are reissued, and the troubleshooting clip goes on telling people to do the thing that was wrong, which is worse than no clip because it is trusted and it is specific. That is the same problem ops/artefacts.py already solves for a PDF, so a module is recorded there against the fingerprints of the design and the canonical tutorial it was cut from: when the design moves the clip is stale by the same mechanism the chart is, and the hourly sentinel that finds one finds the others rather than somebody remembering that videos exist. Repurposing is checked rather than assumed: each module names the platforms whose shape it genuinely fits, and a twelve-minute technique explanation cut to fifteen seconds is refused as a trailer for nothing -- it converts nobody and costs the same to make. The troubleshooting modules are seeded from growth/clusters.py's questions, which are the problems makers demonstrably reported, so a clip about a problem nobody has had is refused and only a problem seen at least three times is planned for. /api/video. Remaining and parked: there is no video capability, no channel and no audience, so a module here is a plan -- what it covers, what it was cut from, where it may go. Assisted conversion needs a visit that ends in an order and support reduction needs cases on the same pattern before and after the clip existed; both are reported as unmeasurable rather than as zeroes.
title: Video Distribution Flywheel

body: Treat creators as a portfolio, not one-off outreach. Track audience/category fit, attributable traffic, conversion, content quality, proof assets, cost/commission and repeat performance. Scale high-contribution relationships and stop weak ones. Require appropriate disclosure.
note: growth/creators.py's portfolio() treats the roster as positions rather than outreach events, and the trap is in the requirement's second instruction. 'Scale high-contribution relationships and stop weak ones' is correct, and applied to a roster where most relationships are unmeasured it stops the ones nobody got round to measuring -- a null sorts to the bottom of a contribution ranking, and the bottom of the list is where things are cut from. So an unmeasured relationship is classified `unmeasured` and named, never weak: what it calls for is a measurement rather than an ending. One good collaboration is a good collaboration and a track record needs more than one, so a single success holds rather than scales. Free seeding is judged on what it produced rather than what it returned, because there is no spend to divide by. Disclosure is already required at the brief: a paid or affiliate arrangement carries its disclosure in the post the audience reads, in words a reader would recognise. /api/creators. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: contribution and support impact need orders, so today every position reads unmeasured and the portfolio scales and stops nothing -- which is the correct output rather than an empty one.
title: Creator Affiliate Portfolio

body: High-performing physical testers may graduate into ambassadors/creators when appropriate and consensual. Their real finished projects can provide trustworthy proof, colourways and educational content. Separate testing compensation/feedback from public review incentives.
note: growth/creators.py's may_graduate() guards the place where two honest programmes quietly merge into one dishonest one. A tester is paid, or given a sample, to find what is wrong; an ambassador is given a relationship for saying what is good. Under one agreement the test fee becomes a review fee -- and worse, the testing stops working, because a tester whose standing depends on enthusiasm reports fewer defects and the physical sample is the most expensive signal this company buys. So graduation requires demonstrated reliability on the tester roster's own threshold, two separate agreements, and a recorded revocable consent to the second relationship, since consent to test is not consent to advocate and a tester who is simply moved across was never asked. Testing terms that mention anything public -- post, share, review, tag, story, mention, feature -- are refused by name, because such a term makes the fee contingent on it whatever the sentence around it says. That a tester who reports a defect keeps their standing and their fee is stated as a term rather than assumed as a courtesy. /api/creators. Remaining and parked on browser_vision with the rest of the roster: no tester has been recruited, so nobody has graduated.
title: Tester-to-Ambassador Path

body: Where Brambleloop lawfully collects consented email subscribers, operate lifecycle flows: welcome/value, category interest, launch, post-purchase support, cross-sell and seasonal reactivation. Segment by demonstrated interest and frequency-cap communications. Track incremental contribution, not open rate vanity.
note: growth/tools.py carries the six lifecycle flows and the requirement's instruction to track incremental contribution rather than open-rate vanity -- the second half made structural. There is no open-rate field and no function returns one, because an open is not a business outcome and has not been a reliable signal since mail clients began fetching images on the reader's behalf; a flow judged on opens is optimised toward subject lines and away from the purchase. Incremental contribution has the harder condition every lifecycle programme skips: a flow sent to everybody measures the people who were going to buy anyway, so without a holdout there is no incremental anything -- and growth/experiments.py already says which designs support a causal claim, so the check is delegated there rather than restated. A segment must come from something the subscriber did or said; a segment built on an open is a segment built on whether somebody's mail client fetched an image. The frequency cap is enforced on the recipient rather than the flow, because five flows that each send politely once a week send five times a week to the person who is in all five, and every flow's own report looks reasonable. Every send goes through growth/owned.py's CASL gate, which is not restated. /api/tools. Remaining and parked on owned_surfaces: no subscriber exists and nothing can be sent.
title: Email / Owned Audience Lifecycle

body: Measure 30/60/90/180-day repeat rate by first product/category/season. Recommend relevant next projects, matching collections and future-season products. Customer lifetime contribution becomes a first-class growth metric.
note: repeat purchase engine; needs customers
title: Repeat Purchase Engine

body: Research whether a recurring pattern club, seasonal collection pass or membership would create genuine customer value and predictable revenue. Do not launch by assumption. Validate demand, support burden, delivery cadence and platform/channel feasibility first.
note: commerce/club.py holds the instruction not to launch by assumption, and names what the appeal hides. A club is the most attractive thing a small shop can imagine -- predictable revenue, a reason to make things, buyers who have already decided -- and the direction the money flows makes it a liability before it is income: payment for work that does not exist yet, and the only product where failing to deliver costs more than the sale, because the people owed are the ones who liked this shop enough to commit. The four questions are not equal. Demand and support burden need buyers, platform feasibility needs a policy read, but delivery cadence is answerable today from how long this company's own work actually takes -- and it is the one that ends clubs. Month one ships what already existed; month two needs a new pattern, certified, on a date somebody else chose. check_cadence() requires 1.3x headroom, because a club that exactly fits its period has no room for the week somebody is ill and there is always that week. may_launch() separates unanswered from answered no, since neither is a launch and only one of them is a finding. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: three of the four questions need buyers or a credential.
title: Collection Subscription / Club Research Lane

body: Where technically feasible and commercially valuable, explore controlled customization: colour planners, size selection, initials/names, motif arrangements or printable project variants. Keep canonical pattern truth intact and price/value-test personalization rather than giving away expensive complexity.
note: products/personalisation.py gives 'keep canonical pattern truth intact' a precise reading in a system where a pattern is a compiled artefact. Every customisation is one of two things: a presentation choice, which changes what the buyer is shown and not what the instructions say -- a colourway, a size from a range the pattern already grades, a large-print or chart-only layout -- leaving the CIR untouched and the certificate covering it; or a construction choice, which changes the instructions and is a new design wearing the old one's name. Letters are stitches: initials change the chart, the counts and the fabric around them, and a name is a different chart for every buyer. A rearranged motif is a different chart and a different fabric at the edges. The failure this prevents is the one every shop makes -- offering custom initials, delivering a hand-edited PDF, and selling it under a certified product's name, so the buyer's copy is the only one nobody checked and the one most likely to be wrong because it is the only one edited by hand. A construction choice is therefore routed rather than refused: it becomes a product, goes through compile, twin, geometry, write, reverse and certificate, and is sold as that. The pricing follows the same line rather than being left to whoever writes the listing: a presentation choice costs nothing per order and charging for it is charging for the listing rather than for work, while a construction choice costs a full chain run per order and giving it away is exactly the expensive complexity the requirement says not to give away. Remaining and parked on live_listings: no customisation can be offered until something is listed.
title: Personalization / Customization Layer

body: Build useful free utilities that attract high-intent makers: yarn/yardage helpers, colour planners, size calculators, project-time estimators, seasonal make-time planners or motif preview tools. Each tool must have a useful standalone purpose and a measured path to relevant Brambleloop products.
note: growth/tools.py holds the requirement's own condition -- a useful standalone purpose and a measured path to a product -- and refuses the failure that is specific and common: the tool that withholds its answer until somebody hands over an email address. That is not a useful utility with a path; it is a lead capture form wearing a calculator's name, and the maker who wanted the number leaves knowing this shop asks for things before it gives them. An address may be asked for after the answer, to save it or to send the pattern it points at, never as its price. The second finding is more useful than the module: five of the six tools the requirement names are arithmetic this system already runs on every release -- yardage per colour from the twin, finished size from the compiler and the twin, make time from the lead-time engine, the last practical make date from the seasonal calendar, and colourway contrast from publish/substitution.py -- so the table names where each already lives rather than proposing to build the calculators again. Only the motif preview needs anything new, and it needs the visual pipeline. What is missing is a surface to put them on, which is one owner action rather than five engineering ones. /api/tools. Remaining and parked on owned_surfaces: there is nowhere to host a tool.
title: Free Tool Acquisition Layer

body: Test legitimate referral/share mechanics that encourage customers to show finished projects or share useful products without manipulating reviews. Track attributable new customers and contribution. Never condition support or discounts on positive reviews.
note: commerce/referral.py draws the same line this build has drawn twice, arriving from a third direction: a reward is for an action -- showing what you made, however it went, or passing something on -- and never for an outcome statement. The refused phrases are commerce/reviews.py's own, imported rather than listed again, because one list is one rule. The second refusal is about counting: 'tell a friend' produces no evidence, so new customers arrive and whoever likes the programme attributes them to it -- a mechanic that cannot be judged will be judged anyway, favourably, by the person who proposed it, so one without an attributable trigger is refused before it runs rather than argued about afterwards. The third is arithmetic: a reward is a cost per acquired customer and is checked against contribution rather than revenue, because a CA$5 credit against a CA$6 pattern is a customer acquired at a loss that looks like growth in every report stopping at the top line. An unmeasured programme is reported as unmeasured, since it is the one everybody remembers fondly. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: no customer exists to refer anybody.
title: Product-Led Referral Research

body: Analyze legitimate review themes and star distribution against listing conversion and repeat behavior. Identify what buyers praise, misunderstand or wish existed. Feed findings into product design, PDFs, listing claims and support. Never fabricate, purchase or gate reviews.
note: commerce/reviews.py reads this shop's own reviews, and the prohibition's third verb is the one worth being precise about. Gating is not buying: it is withholding something the buyer already paid for -- the file, the answer, the fix -- until they leave a rating, and it does not feel like buying a review because no money moves. That is the version a small shop actually commits, usually by accident, in a support template that says 'if this helped, a review would mean a lot' attached to the thing they were owed anyway, so check_support_copy() refuses eight such phrases by name. Nothing in the module writes a review. The analytical half has an arithmetic problem the rule does not: a shop with three reviews has a rating one bad day away from 3.7 and the first handful dominate the average for a year, so the star distribution is refused below twenty rather than reported with a caveat -- a caveat is read once and an average is read every week, and the number would move somebody to redesign a product over one person's experience. Themes stay readable when the average is not, on intel/observe.py's RECURRING_AT. The most useful output is the routing rather than the counting: a theme in the misunderstood category is usually not a product defect but a disclosure missing from the listing, and commerce/buyer_trust.py already holds the list a purchase needs -- routing a misunderstanding to the design queue rewrites a pattern that was correct. Praise routes to listing claims, which may say it because a buyer said it first; a wish routes to product selection. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: this shop has no reviews.
title: Review-to-Conversion Learning

body: With explicit permission, build a gallery of real customer/tester finished projects linked to exact pattern versions and yarn/colour notes. Use as trust/proof, inspiration and support material. Measure whether proof improves conversion.
note: commerce/buyer_trust.py's customer_gallery() adds the thing #258 is actually about: an entry belongs to a pattern version. A customer's photograph of v1.0.0 shown beside a listing selling v1.2.0 is proof of a different object, and it is the most believable wrong thing on the page because it is real -- so it is marked rather than removed, since it is the strongest evidence this shop can hold. The colourway is now required, because it is what a browser is choosing from and nothing had required it; the yarn is not on that list because record_image() already refuses a physical photograph without one, and the gallery's consent check is named as a second line rather than the line for the same reason. proof_lift() refuses to say whether proof improved conversion without both arms -- a gallery added to every listing measures the month it was added -- and growth/experiments.py decides whether the result may be called causal or an association. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: no customer or tester photograph exists, so the gallery is empty rather than thin, and nothing has permission to be shown because nothing has been taken.
title: Customer Project Gallery

body: During the first 100 customers, prioritize flawless downloads, rapid support, truthful expectations, defect prevention and post-purchase clarity. Do not sacrifice contribution irrationally, but treat early trust as a compounding asset.
note: commerce/first_hundred.py reframes the sprint, and the reframing is the work. Read as written the requirement produces a plan that starts on the day of the first sale, and that is the wrong day for four of its five priorities. A flawless download is a property of the delivery path and the first buyer either gets the file or does not; truthful expectations are written into a listing before anybody reads it; defect prevention is the release chain, which runs before a product exists to sell; post-purchase clarity is a page and a file, either written or not. Only rapid support genuinely needs customers, because it is a response time and there is nothing to respond to yet. So four priorities are checkable today and are not waiting for anybody -- which matters because the alternative is comfortable: a plan beginning at the first sale lets all four sit unfinished while the shop feels prepared, and the first hundred customers are the review base, the repeat base and the proof base, each arriving exactly once. The sprint ends at a hundred, stated because a permanent sprint is just how the company works and calling it a sprint is how nobody asks when the extra cost stops. 'Do not sacrifice contribution irrationally' reads specifically: the sprint may spend support hours, sample costs and a slower release cadence, and may not spend the price -- a discount teaches the hundred buyers whose repeat behaviour matters most that the price is negotiable, and they are exactly the cohort the value ladder depends on. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: rapid support has nothing to respond to, and the four that do not need a customer are currently all unready.
title: New-Shop Trust Sprint

body: Invite a small voluntary sample of legitimate buyers/testers to provide structured feedback on why they clicked, why they bought, what nearly stopped them, pattern clarity and what they want next. No reward is contingent on positive sentiment. Convert responses into hypotheses.
note: growth/interviews.py builds the instrument and refuses the three ways a voluntary sample is decided in advance. Selection rules that can see the outcome are refused by name -- 'left a good review', 'repeat buyer', 'no refund requested' all describe themselves as asking your best customers, and all of them pre-select the answer; only frames blind to the outcome are permitted. The incentive lives on the invitation and must be identical across a round, because an incentive chosen after reading a response is contingent on sentiment whatever was intended: contingency is a question of ordering, not of motive. 'What nearly stopped you' carries a 14-day recall window and a later answer is kept as reconstructed, since a hesitation is rebuilt rather than retrieved. Nothing here ever produces a finding: the output is hypotheses, labelled in the data, and the only promotion route runs through an instrument that asked nobody a question -- another interview is refused by name. Invitations go through the CASL gate on the purchase relationship. Remaining and parked on the customers gate: a round needs buyers to invite, and a survey of testers alone answers a question about testers.
title: First-100-Customer Interview Sampling

body: Regularly audit the buyer journey from Etsy search/listing through digital download and support. Identify confusion around 'pattern vs finished item', file access, terminology, skill, sizing and included deliverables. Fix recurring friction in listing and product packaging.
note: commerce/friction.py files friction at the stage that caused it rather than the stage it arrived at. That is the substance: nearly all of it arrives at support and almost none of it is made there, so an audit grouped by arrival produces a better support macro while the listing goes on telling the next four hundred people the same thing. Correctness friction acts at n=1 and comprehension friction needs a rate, not a count -- three in five is an emergency, three in four hundred is three people. The five listing-caused confusions are auditable today against the listing artefact, and the audit reads the artefact rather than asking seo.build_description whether its own output is correct; a test asserts the shop's generated copy passes its own auditor. A stage with no complaints and no traversals reads not_yet_walked, never clean, because zero complaints from zero buyers is identical evidence to a flawless funnel. Remaining and parked on the live_listings gate: search, decision, delivery, first use and support are facts about a journey somebody walked, and the non-buyers whose friction costs most are outside every instrument here by construction.
title: Checkout / Purchase-Friction Audit

body: Compare forecast versus actual weekly/monthly revenue by channel/category. Decompose error into traffic, CTR, conversion, AOV, repeat, launch timing and winner rate. Continuously recalibrate the CA$5K trajectory model; optimistic model error reduces confidence automatically.
note: scale/calibration.py makes three things structural. A forecast carries made_on and it must precede the period it predicts: recalibrating against expectations recorded afterwards produces a model that is always well calibrated and never right, because the expectation adjusts to the outcome on the way past and nobody notices. The error is decomposed in log space, not by a waterfall -- substituting terms one at a time through a product gives each term a different share depending where in the sequence it is walked, so whoever does it picks, after seeing the numbers, how much of the miss belongs to the term they would rather blame; log space is exact and order-independent, and an unmeasured term lands in `unexplained` rather than being distributed onto the measured ones. And optimism is penalised five times as hard as pessimism, automatically, with recovery gated behind three consecutive accurate periods, because symmetric recovery lets one good month erase a year of forecasting high. The output is a ceiling applied to scale.confidence.probability, never a second probability: two answers to one question means the flattering one gets quoted. Remaining and parked on the live_listings gate: a period with no live listings is excluded rather than scored, which is every period today -- calibrating on them would report a catastrophically optimistic model, which is arithmetic about an unopened shop rather than a finding.
title: Revenue Forecast Calibration

body: Track leading indicators before revenue arrives: qualified impressions, CTR, favourites/cart signals where available, conversion, bundle attach, email/content traffic, creator traffic, search trend direction, support defects and release velocity. Avoid declaring success from leading indicators without orders.
note: the constraint solver and loop registry expose the leading indicators that exist. Remaining and parked on the live_listings gate: impressions, click-through and favourites are facts about a listing somebody can see, and no credential produces them for a listing that was never published. That gate counts an Etsy listing id rather than reading the phase flag, because a phase is a statement of intent and a listing id is a listing.
title: Leading Indicator Dashboard

body: Each week, identify ONE primary commercial constraint and a small number of secondary constraints. Reallocate experiments/agents toward the constraint with highest expected marginal contribution. Examples: insufficient qualified traffic, weak thumbnail CTR, weak conversion, low AOV, low repeat or product gap.
note: the weekly constraint solver ranks the four terms by expected monthly contribution per week of effort rather than by distance from target, because the biggest gap is often the slowest to close. With every term at zero it says so plainly: the product of zeros cannot be moved by one term.
title: Weekly Growth Constraint Solver
