body: Maintain a diversified experiment portfolio with expected value, cost, duration, sample requirement, owner, stop rule and result. Balance quick low-cost tests with strategic longer tests. Kill experiments that cannot change a decision.
note: experiments carry expected cost, duration, sample requirement and stop rule, and undersampled results are unclaimable rather than provisional.
title: Growth Experiment Portfolio

body: Whenever possible, distinguish incremental revenue from revenue that would have occurred anyway. Use holdouts, staggered rollouts, pre/post controls or channel attribution. Do not credit a discount, ad or creator with all observed sales merely because it was active.
note: the design decides what may be claimed: holdout and staggered rollout support a causal claim, pre/post does not -- it cannot separate the change from the week it happened in, and seasonality is the largest effect in this business. Recorded as association, in the record rather than in a caveat.
title: Incrementality Discipline

body: Shift product and marketing capacity based on time-to-event and make-time. Early season favors complex flagships; late season favors quick makes, giftables and digital last-minute projects. Roll capacity forward before demand collapses.
note: most of this requirement was already built: seasonal/compression.py retires lanes one at a time and moves each closing lane's share into the fastest lane still open, so the early-flagship to late-quick-make shift falls out of the arithmetic rather than out of somebody remembering it in November, and next_year_track starts next year's flagship under a cap. What was missing is the word 'and' in 'product and marketing capacity', and it is not a detail: the two run on different clocks. Engineering leaves an occasion when its last lane closes -- nothing new could be launched, indexed and finished in time. Marketing leaves weeks later, at the buyer's own last practical make date, because the catalogue already listed goes on selling until then, and those weeks are the ones that earn most. seasonal/rollforward.py holds the two as separate ledgers over one calendar and states the rule: engineering rolls forward first, marketing rolls forward last. Roll-forward is refused in both directions -- nothing leaves an occasion that still holds it, and engineering may not arrive at one inside its own preparation lead, because capacity moved out of a season that is ending into one that is already late has been spent on being late twice. demand_curve() computes the structural floor (past the last practical make date demand is zero because nobody can finish the object) and reports the decay before it as unobserved: makers do not all wait for the last day, but no listing of this shop's has been watched through a season, and a decay date taken from a plausible curve is a point estimate presented as a fact.
title: Seasonal Capacity Arbitrage

body: Where Etsy data and policy permit, distinguish Canada, U.S. and other meaningful buyer markets for terminology, holidays, timing and pricing/currency effects. Do not assume Canadian search behavior represents Etsy globally.
note: commerce/markets.py distinguishes Canada, the United States and everywhere else for the two things that are genuinely different for a digital pattern, and states the one that is not. Terminology: a US double crochet is a UK treble, so the same words name different stitches and a pattern that does not say which it uses makes the wrong fabric for the buyers who read it the other way. The writer already emits both; what was missing is which buyer needs which. Holidays: Canadian Thanksgiving is the second Monday of October and American Thanksgiving the fourth Thursday of November -- six weeks apart, different shopping windows, and a product merchandised to one is merchandised away from the other; the calendar this system carries holds the Canadian date, which is correct for this company and incomplete for its market. UK Mothering Sunday is roughly two months before the Canadian and American date. Delivery does not differ at all, and that is stated rather than assumed, because a digital file arriving the same day everywhere is the one cross-border advantage this business has. The requirement's closing instruction is not to assume Canadian search behaviour represents Etsy globally, and the error actually present points the other way, which is easier to miss: the benchmark is a United States shop, so every term frequency this system has measured is American, and reading it as Canadian or as global is the same mistake with the countries swapped. The module labels it rather than discarding it, because American behaviour is still the largest Etsy buyer market's. Pricing and currency are #269. Remaining and parked on benchmark_observation: correcting the label needs a benchmark in another market, which is an owner decision about which shops to observe rather than a capability this build can grant itself. /api/markets.
title: Cross-Border Demand Lens

body: Normalize product economics into a canonical reporting currency while preserving transaction currency, platform/payment fees, regulatory/currency conversion fees and ad fees. Pricing decisions use net contribution, not sticker price.
note: finance/currency.py normalises into CAD while preserving the transaction's own currency, and preserving is the word doing the work: converting a USD sale and keeping only the CAD figure destroys the one number that can later be reconciled against a bank statement, and books that cannot be reconciled will be argued with. Every amount carries the currency it happened in, every conversion carries the rate and the date it was taken, and an assumed rate says it is assumed -- a converted figure whose rate is invisible is indistinguishable from a measured one. A currency with no rate on file is refused rather than converted at something plausible. Two fee classes the previous model did not name are now priced: currency conversion, which never appears as a line item and appears instead as a slightly worse rate, and regulatory operating fees charged as a percentage of the order total. Both default to zero and the zero is honest -- they are listed under fees_not_yet_observed, because a margin computed without a fee should say so rather than look like one that included it. Net contribution is returned before the sticker price, which is the requirement's closing sentence made structural rather than remembered. /api/finance.
title: Currency / Fee Margin Normalization

body: Model loss of the top SKU, top seasonal event or top traffic channel. If CA$5K collapses under one plausible failure, create a diversification plan. Breakout exploitation remains aggressive, but resilience becomes part of the confidence score.
note: three plausible single failures -- top SKU, top family, top three -- each with the shortfall it would leave against the target. Exploiting a winner stays aggressive; this measures what losing it would cost, so resilience is part of the confidence rather than an afterthought.
title: Revenue Concentration Stress Test

body: Maintain a registry of growth loops with evidence strength: Etsy organic, Pinterest, Google/SEO, creators, email/repeat, paid ads, bundles/cross-sells, free tools/content. Record cost, latency, scalability, contribution and confidence. CA$5K confidence rises as independent loops become proven.
note: growth/loops.py registers seven loops with derived strength: untested, attempted, measured, repeatable. Strength is earned from recorded traffic rather than assigned, only measured and repeatable count as evidence, and a strength claimed on twelve visits is refused. The CA$5K acquisition rung now reads this registry rather than taking a caller's number.
title: Inventory of Proven Growth Loops

body: Before aggressively scaling a product/channel, require product quality stable, support/refunds acceptable, truthful creative certified, contribution positive or intentionally bounded, attribution working and capacity to handle resulting customer support. Growth cannot outrun product truth.
note: six scale conditions, all required. A product that converts well and generates support tickets is ready to be fixed, not scaled -- scaling multiplies whatever is already true.
title: Scale Readiness Gate

body: Maintain multiple transparent scenarios, e.g. 250 orders x CA$20 AOV, 200 x CA$25, 167 x CA$30, plus mixed Etsy/direct/repeat compositions. Derive required visits from observed conversion and include fees/refunds/ads for contribution. The CEO chooses the most evidence-supported path, not the prettiest spreadsheet.
note: the scenario matrix is computed, sorted by the traffic each path needs, and every row records whether its conversion rate was observed and over what sample. Evidence-supported paths are counted separately and today the count is zero -- with the note saying the most attractive row is the one to distrust, because it is attractive on account of its assumptions rather than its difficulty.
title: $5K Scenario Matrix

body: Track: product-quality confidence -> demand confidence -> conversion confidence -> acquisition confidence -> AOV confidence -> repeat confidence -> portfolio resilience. The modeled probability cannot exceed the weakest critical layer without explicit justification.
note: the ladder is a minimum over the critical layers, never an average: an average lets six strong rungs hide one fatal one, and 'we can make it, price it and nobody buys it' is exactly that shape. Tested with a company strong everywhere except acquisition -- the average reads above 0.7 and the model reports 0.0.
title: $5K Confidence Ladder

body: A >=75% internal modeled probability for sustainable CA$5K/month requires at minimum: several independently selling products across more than one product family; a meaningful sample of real outside customers; stable low defect/refund/support severity; positive contribution after known fees; repeatable qualified acquisition; observed bundle/AOV behavior; some repeat purchase evidence or a robust substitute; seasonal/evergreen balance; and downside scenarios that remain near the target. Thresholds adapt to actual data rather than being gamed.
note: the evidence standard is six counts (selling SKUs, product families, outside customers, orders, acquisition loops, months of history) and the modelled figure is capped at 0.74 until all six are met. Tested both ways: unmet caps a maximal ladder, and met allows a genuinely high number, because a model that can only ever report near zero would stop being read.
title: 75%+ $5K Evidence Standard

body: Once real sales exist, create a permanent CEO/CFO/Growth/Product war-room view showing current monthly run rate, 30-day forecast, gap to CA$5K, primary constraint, top five actions by expected incremental contribution, experiments in flight, winner alerts, risk concentration and owner approvals. Agents execute from this board continuously. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.4.2 - Proven-Trend Seasonal Capture & Lead-Time Engine NON-NEGOTIABLE owner requirement: aggressively learn from proven benchmark product markets and visual merchandising, transform those opportunities for upcoming seasons/holidays, and release early enough that customers can buy AND physically make the project before the intended event. Brambleloop independently engineers its patterns and creates its own listing assets.
note: CA$5K war room; needs real sales
title: $5K War Room

body: Brambleloop must continuously observe MJsOffTheHookDesigns and the elite benchmark panel for commercially successful product concepts, silhouettes, product families, merchandising mechanisms, palette directions and seasonal movement. Proven demand is an instruction to compete, not a reason to avoid the category. The system should enter the same broad/generic product market aggressively while engineering Brambleloop's own pattern and producing its own visual assets.
note: proven-trend capture depends on MJs observation
title: NON-NEGOTIABLE: Proven-Trend Seasonal Capture

body: Accessible competitor listing photography is first-class market evidence. Browser/vision pods extract silhouette, proportions, neckline, sleeve treatment, stripe/blocking logic, colour architecture, styling, setting, product scale, shot sequence, seasonal cues and apparent customer promise. These observations feed concept generation. Do not copy the competitor's actual photograph or reproduce protected pattern instructions.
note: visual listing intelligence; needs browser/vision
title: Visual Listing Intelligence Is a Product Input

body: For every proven evergreen or current benchmark concept, automatically evaluate season/holiday transformations. Examples include changing palette, styling, motif vocabulary, trim, gift context, collection story and supporting accessories for Christmas, Halloween, Easter, Valentine's, Mother's/Father's Day where relevant, fall, winter, spring, summer and other evidence-supported events. Transformations must remain technically coherent and commercially desirable.
note: creative/seasonal_transform.py routes every transformation before it is costed. Palette, styling, gift context and collection story change what a buyer sees and nothing a maker makes, so they re-merchandise (#292's path, which already refuses to count them as catalogue growth). Motif vocabulary, trim and a companion accessory change the object, so they take a new CIR, a compile and a physical test -- and therefore have to be worth them: an engineered variant with no emotional promise is refused by name, because the creative jury's dominant failure on the Build-1 catalogue was exactly that and a seasonal palette does not fix it. Motifs outside the occasion's grammar are refused, and a variant built only from the saturated motifs is named as the commodity. derive() mints a child concept only from an engineering route with no unresolved problems, and the child faces the jury on its own. /api/seasonal/transform.
title: Seasonal Transformation Engine

body: Maintain dated seasonal palette intelligence from current marketplace evidence, fashion/home signals and Brambleloop performance. Each product concept can receive multiple seasonally appropriate colourways. Colour changes are treated as merchandising/product variants only when the underlying pattern truth supports them; imagery and listing claims must match the actual colourway.
note: seasonal/colour.py builds the layer from evidence that was already free and already collected: Etsy publishes per-image hex, hue, saturation and brightness, so every audited benchmark listing carries the colours its photographs actually contain and the date they were read. That is what dated marketplace intelligence means here -- a count of what a proven seller in this department is photographed in, with an observation window, rather than a forecast somebody wrote. A palette with no window is a claim about taste; one with a window is a measurement that can be seen to have gone stale. Below five audited listings it reports unmeasurable with the count, because a palette read from fewer is one photographer's habit and an empty palette reported as neutral would let a colourway decision rest on nothing. propose_colourway() takes exactly the number of colours the pattern already has and skips any swatch that would merge with one already chosen, using the same lightness threshold the substitution guide and the value stack use because it is the same failure in three places; a palette that cannot supply enough separable colours is refused rather than topped up from elsewhere, since filling the rest would put colours in a listing this market has not been seen using. is_variant() holds the requirement's own condition: a colour change is a merchandising variant only while the pattern truth is unchanged -- same colour count, same roles -- and a two-colour pattern given a three-colour way is a different pattern wearing this one's name, which is how a catalogue's version accounting stops meaning anything. A colourway stated in words is refused, because it cannot be checked against what a photograph shows. Remaining: of the three sources the requirement names, marketplace evidence is here; external fashion and home signals need a feed nobody has connected, and this company's own colour performance needs sales. Both are named rather than filled with something plausible, because a forecast resting on one source presented as resting on three is the most confident kind of wrong. /api/colour.
title: Colour-Forecast Layer

body: When an MJs/elite listing demonstrates a strong generic market concept, route it to the relevant specialist pod. Decompose why the product appears commercially strong, generate Brambleloop responses for the current and upcoming seasonal windows, run Creative Supremacy/benchmark gates, engineer the selected original pattern through CIR, generate Brambleloop-owned assets, then launch/advertise according to evidence.
note: MJs-to-Brambleloop response pipeline; needs MJs evidence
title: MJs-to-Brambleloop Seasonal Response Pipeline

body: A proven broad concept such as a cropped V-neck button-front striped crochet cardigan may trigger Brambleloop variants for upcoming demand: Christmas palettes (e.g. forest/cranberry/cream/gold), winter palettes, spring palettes, fall palettes and other evidence-supported themes. Preserve commercially useful generic characteristics while Brambleloop independently engineers construction, grading and instructions and creates its own model-led photography.
note: the master's worked example is a function rather than a paragraph: striped_cardigan_example() runs the proven cropped cardigan through the engine and returns three seasonal palettes routed as re-merchandising -- one cardigan photographed three times, zero new patterns -- beside one engineered Christmas variant that changes what the garment depicts, carries a nostalgic promise delivered by the motif, and grounds a WOW mechanism in the yoke's own increases. catalogue_growth is 1, not 4. Running it as code means the answer comes from the rules rather than from whoever is reading them.
title: Example Transformation - Striped Cardigan

body: Seasonal demand planning must work backward from when the CUSTOMER needs the finished object, not merely the holiday date. Estimate project make-time distribution by product/skill level, buyer planning/shopping lead time, tester/QA time, Etsy indexing/learning time, creative production time and advertising ramp. Complex products must launch substantially earlier than quick makes.
note: make-time is an interval (seasonal/uncertainty.py) rather than a point estimate; the spread is asymmetric, narrows only with recorded physical samples, and never collapses to a point
title: Maker Lead-Time Is Mandatory

body: For every event, compute: EVENT DATE minus customer completion buffer minus estimated make time minus purchase/planning buffer minus marketplace discovery/ramp buffer = target latest effective launch date. Also calculate preferred launch date with additional learning/optimization time. Recompute as observed buyer behavior improves estimates.
note: the backward chain now carries optimistic and pessimistic launch dates, and feasibility() grades a window as comfortable/tight/high-risk/infeasible with infeasible reserved for a passed optimistic bound
title: Seasonal Launch-Date Compiler

body: Classify products by customer make-time: QUICK (hours/1-2 days), SHORT (several days), MEDIUM (roughly 1-2 weeks), LONG (multi-week), FLAGSHIP (potentially many weeks). Seasonal scheduling gives LONG/FLAGSHIP products the earliest runway and can continue QUICK products much closer to the event.
note: the five lanes with make-hour bands, and the runway ordering falls out of the arithmetic rather than being imposed: a flagship's make time pushes its latest launch earlier by construction.
title: Complexity-Based Seasonal Lanes

body: Maintain a continuously rolling calendar rather than separate one-off 'Christmas strike teams.' Every day, look 30/60/90/120/180/365 days ahead for holidays, seasons, gifting moments and cultural/market events relevant to crochet. Each event has research, concept, engineering, test, asset, launch, optimization and late-season quick-make phases.
note: seasonal/calendar.py rolls: an event that has passed is next year's, so Christmas is 364 days away on Boxing Day rather than vanishing for eleven months. All six horizons index into one event list rather than duplicating it, and each event carries the phase its distance implies -- research, concept, engineering, test, assets, launch, optimise, late quick make, closed. The phase boundaries come from the lead-time engine's arithmetic, not from taste.
title: Rolling 365-Day Opportunity Calendar

body: Create persistent or on-demand specialist strike teams for major commercially relevant events. Christmas, Halloween, Easter and major seasons receive deep dedicated coverage; additional events are created when demand evidence supports them. Teams own opportunity maps, product gaps, colour/motif language, deadlines, benchmark changes and revenue targets.
note: seasonal/teams.py gives Christmas, Halloween and Easter standing teams and requires recorded demand evidence -- rows in the learning radar or observed listings, counted against a floor -- before any fourth event earns one, because a team is cheap to create and expensive to staff. A team is a share of capacity or it is a name: shares are checked against what exists, a team holding nothing is refused as an org-chart entry, and 25% is reserved for evergreen work because a seasonal programme that consumes everything leaves a shop excellent in December and absent in February. Overlapping occasions scale proportionally rather than overrunning, keeping the order the compression programmes established. A team whose occasion has passed the buyer's last practical make date releases its capacity automatically, which is how the next occasion gets staffed without a manual rebalance, and a priority programme with neither a team nor a recorded reason is refused. /api/seasonal/teams.
title: Seasonal Strike Teams by Event

body: Do not reduce an event to one blanket. For each major event, explore the full maker/gift ecosystem: garments, stockings, ornaments, tree/table decor, wreaths, coasters, baskets, pillows, throws, bags, hats, accessories, amigurumi, quick gifts, bundles and other technically/market appropriate categories. Portfolio selection remains evidence-driven.
note: depth is measured against the departments an event actually spans rather than against a product count, because six Christmas products say nothing about whether five are blankets. seasonal/depth.py turns each gap into a brief: the forms that serve the department, the make lane each form implies, whether that lane can still launch for this event, the family roles it would fill and the last optimistic launch date. A department whose forms are all past their window is reported as next season's gap rather than this season's work, and hurry is kept apart from stop. A brief is not a product: nothing here counts as coverage, and depth moves only when something is built. /api/seasonal/depth.
title: Holiday Portfolio Depth

body: Products should form coherent collections where useful. A winning seasonal visual language can extend across multiple original products and price points, enabling cross-sell and bundle behavior. Collections share palette/story but each product must stand on its own commercially.
note: seasonal/collections.py checks coherence and originality as opposing constraints, which is what makes this more than a naming convention. Members must carry the collection's palette and story, because that is what a buyer recognises across a grid; and they must differ structurally, measured by the concept engine's own distance() -- which scores a pure recolour at zero because palette is not a term in it, so a derivative is refused by the same arithmetic that refuses a duplicate in a tournament field. The closest pair is reported rather than the mean: one derivative pair makes a derivative collection and an average hides it. A collection needs three members (two is a product and its accessory) across at least two make lanes, because cross-sell is the commercial argument and it needs somewhere cheap to enter and somewhere dearer to move to. assemble() builds the largest coherent collection from candidates, greedy by lane breadth since that is the constraint that actually binds, and names what it rejected and why.
title: Seasonal Collection Architecture

body: Every observed trend receives an estimated half-life: flash/meme, short seasonal, recurring seasonal, multi-season fashion, or evergreen. Development effort and launch urgency depend on half-life. Do not spend flagship engineering time on a trend likely to expire before customers can finish the project.
note: every trend carries a half-life and the half-life caps the make lane it may justify: a flash trend cannot buy FLAGSHIP engineering. A refusal rather than a ranking penalty, because multi-week work on something that expires before a customer could finish it costs the window as well as the work. An unclassified trend is refused outright.
title: Trend Half-Life Classification

body: When a high-confidence trend is time-sensitive and technically simple, use a fast lane with bounded scope, deterministic validation and rapid asset production. Fast does not bypass pattern truth, IP/policy, visual truth or customer safety/quality gates.
note: seasonal/fastlane.py admits a candidate only when the evidence is confident, the trend's half-life can repay the work (the calendar's own rule, reused rather than restated), the make lane is SHORT or faster, the risk class is one the compiler verifies completely, and the product is one component, at most three colours and no technique the catalogue has never used -- because a new technique needs a physical sample and a sample is the one part of this company nobody can hurry. What the lane buys is scope, never checking. The gates it runs are the release chain's own CANONICAL_STAGES, imported rather than retyped, because a second copy of that list is exactly how the guarantee quietly stops being true; a test also scans certificate.py and asserts the constant matches the stages the chain actually appends. Product-conditional stages stay conditional on the product and never on the lane, and a release missing any owed gate is refused by name. /api/seasonal/fastlane.
title: Fast Response Lane

body: Periodically inspect proven Brambleloop evergreen products for legitimate seasonal re-merchandising opportunities: new colourways, styled photography, bundles, compatible add-ons and seasonal search positioning. Avoid unnecessary new pattern SKUs when the pattern itself is unchanged; preserve clean version/product accounting.
note: seasonal/remerchandising.py lists the five moves the requirement names -- colourway, styled photography, bundle, add-on, seasonal search positioning -- and refuses any that changes construction, form, rows, stitch counts, gauge or the release hash, because that is a new product and a different pipeline with a tournament, a compile and a physical test in it. No move increments the catalogue: a recolour presented as a launch inflates catalogue size, release rate and the apparent breadth of a collection at once. 'Proven' is a claim about sales and this company has none, so candidates are eligible rather than proven and every row says which. capabilities() computes which of the five moves the company can actually take rather than taking the list from its caller -- the same shape as a gate reading a configured variable instead of a recorded success. search_positioning became genuinely available on 2026-09-20, when the benchmark credential made a department's observed buyer language countable. The seasonal.remerchandising cadence runs the inspection weekly against the soonest proven occasion, because 'periodically inspect' is a cadence and a review that never runs is the same as one that does not exist. bundle_pairs() turns 'bundle: available' into concrete pairs: which two products, why a buyer wants both, and which half is the add-on (the faster lane, because a small make beside a longer one is an easy yes). A product is never bundled with itself in another colour -- the catalogue-inflation move this module refuses, wearing a bundle label -- and a pair with no stated reason is refused, because 'both exist' is not a reason and a bundle built on it is a discount. A product whose form is unknown is reported unpairable rather than paired on a guess. Remaining: colourway and styled photography wait on image_generation -- a recolour that cannot be shown is not a merchandising move, it is a note -- and 'proven' waits on a sale. Both halves that this build can reach are built, so the requirement is parked rather than ready: it sat at the top of the ready queue as the next-highest-value work while nothing in it could be started. /api/seasonal/remerchandising.
title: Evergreen-to-Seasonal Multiplier

body: Before launch, map each seasonal product to real buyer language from Etsy/market evidence: object + technique + recipient/use + aesthetic + season/event + skill/feature where relevant. Search strategy must reflect what buyers are already seeking while remaining accurate to the product.
note: commerce/intent.py maps a product across the six facets the requirement names and refuses the two ways the map becomes a description of ourselves: a facet carrying our own vocabulary, and a facet made only of words that describe nothing. Object, recipient/use and season/event are required. Every phrase is labelled assumed or observed, promoted only by a recorded Keyword or BenchmarkListing row, and the two are never blended. The credential arrived 2026-09-19 and promotion is live. arena_language() adds the half the requirement asks for and nothing could answer before: for each proven-and-unserved department, the words a shopper actually sees, counted across observed titles and sorted into the six facets, with marketplace furniture separated rather than dropped. Observed by construction; it emits single words and never a title, because term frequency is demand intelligence and a title is somebody's expression. It is not a search-volume claim and says so. /api/search/intent, /api/search/arena-language. Re-audited to covered 2026-09-20: all six facets, the assumed/observed split, credential-driven promotion and per-arena buyer language are implemented and tested. It has not yet been applied to a launched product because nothing is launched, which is a fact about Shadow Mode rather than missing capability.
title: Seasonal Search Intent Mapping

body: Paid acquisition for important seasonal products begins early enough to gather CTR/conversion/CAC evidence and improve creative before peak demand. Do not wait until the event is imminent to discover the thumbnail or offer is weak. Scaling follows the evidence-based CAC/ROAS controls in #242-244.
note: pre-season ad learning, winner scaling; needs ad authority
title: Pre-Season Ad Learning Window

body: If a seasonal product clears quality gates and demonstrates profitable/reasonable acquisition economics, automatically increase creative testing, supporting pins/content, cross-sells, bundles and paid budget within approved scaling bands. Escalate larger spend increases to the owner's mobile approval inbox with exact economics.
note: pre-season ad learning, winner scaling; needs ad authority
title: Aggressive Winner Scaling

body: For each major upcoming event, show days to preferred/latest launch, products by stage, benchmark gaps, search opportunities, projected customer make time, ad learning status, current seasonal revenue/run rate, winner alerts and bottlenecks. The orchestrator reallocates agents toward deadlines and expected contribution.
note: /api/seasonal is the war room and seasonal.sentinel recomputes it daily, naming the at-risk rows rather than counting them and raising a P2 for the soonest. What remains is seasonal revenue, run rate and ad learning status, each of which is a reading of commerce that has not happened. Unmeasured is not zero, so the war room reports them absent.
title: Seasonal Revenue War Room

body: If a product cannot realistically be discovered, purchased and completed before its intended event, do not launch it under a misleading seasonal premise merely because engineering is finished. Pivot it to evergreen/next-season positioning, simplify into a legitimate quick-make derivative, or hold it for the next cycle.
note: LaunchPlan.recommendation() refuses to return 'launch' once the window has closed, and returns pivot-to-evergreen, simplify-to-a-quick-make or hold-for-next-cycle with the reason. Finished engineering is not an argument: the customer cannot finish in time, and the conversion data that comes back would teach the shop the wrong lesson about the category.
title: Missed-Window Kill / Pivot Rule

body: After every major event, analyze which concepts, palettes, categories, thumbnails, search terms, prices, bundles and channels actually worked. Feed evidence into next year's calendar immediately, including when demand began/peaked/decayed and actual customer make-time/support signals.
note: post-season learning harvest; needs a season of data
title: Post-Season Learning Harvest

body: For each major event and department, maintain a matrix of elite-benchmark product markets versus Brambleloop coverage: benchmark concept/category, observed merchandising mechanisms, upcoming seasonal adaptation opportunities, our competing products, quality-gate result, launch date, traffic, conversion and revenue. Use it to expose unserved proven markets.
note: seasonal/benchmark_matrix.py joins the two halves: the calendar's own map of which departments an occasion spans and which this catalogue answers, and the benchmark's depth per department counted from observed listings. The half that was missing arrived on 2026-09-19 when the credential was verified by use and 438 listings were read. The discipline it enforces is narrow and is the reason the requirement is worth having: a department is 'proven and unserved' only when somebody actually looked, because an unobserved market and a market with nothing in it render identically in a matrix -- both as an empty cell -- and the empty cell is the one somebody points at in a planning meeting. Gaps are ordered by how much the benchmark sells there and how soon the occasion is. /api/seasonal/benchmark-matrix.
title: Seasonal Benchmark Coverage Matrix

body: Build 2 must demonstrate an end-to-end simulated seasonal cycle: observe a benchmark market signal, classify generic product characteristics, choose an upcoming event, compute customer lead-time and launch date, generate multiple original seasonal responses, select/engineer one, certify it, create Brambleloop-owned assets, prepare search/ads, and show that the scheduler launched early enough for a customer to make it before the event. This is release-blocking. BRAMBLELOOP QUEUED MASTER UPGRADES v1.4.3 - MJsOffTheHookDesigns Priority Mission HUGE MANDATORY FLAG / NON-NEGOTIABLE OWNER PRIORITY: MJsOffTheHookDesigns is the specifically named anchor benchmark. Brambleloop must maintain dedicated cloud browser/vision intelligence around this shop, learn its commercially successful product markets and visual merchandising, aggressively evaluate those same markets for upcoming seasonal/holiday adaptations, and release early enough for customers to buy and make the project. Brambleloop independently engineers its patterns and creates its own publishable visual assets.
note: seasonal/cycle.py runs the whole cycle the requirement names, in its order, and reports each link's evidence rather than a tick: a benchmark signal somebody recorded, the pods that market is made of, an upcoming event with runway, the customer's lead time chained backwards to a launch date, several original responses, one selected and authored as a CIR, the full release chain run, assets, and search coverage. Verified end to end against a seeded benchmark: 90 listings observed, 5 proven-and-unserved arenas, Halloween/hats at 41 days, 6 concepts proposed, one engineered at a gauge derived from its own yarn, and a certificate granted with the reverse compile among its stages. The clause that makes this an acceptance test rather than a checklist is the last one -- show that the scheduler launched early enough for a customer to make it before the event -- so the cycle ends on that arithmetic and the arithmetic is the verdict. Two defects were found by running it. It first reported complete on a launch date twenty days in the past: the backward chain wanted the product live on 31 August, the cycle measured a buyer's finish from that date, found it comfortable and called the window met. A date that has passed cannot be launched on, so it measures from the earliest date that can be and says the preferred window was missed. And it reported complete for a run with no model provider, which had invented nothing, engineered nothing and certified nothing -- a step the run never reached is absent rather than gated, and absent is not passing, so completeness now requires every named link to have been reached. The verdict is the weakest link rather than a count of green steps, because a backward-chained schedule is exactly the structure where an average hides one broken link, and a gate that stopped the run outranks the steps it stopped: those are consequences and the gate is what somebody can act on. Remaining and parked: photographic and styled imagery needs image_generation, and paid media needs ad_authority -- both are named as gated rather than simulated, because a placeholder product photograph would make the cycle green and prove nothing, and is the one thing the asset-truth gate exists to refuse one level down. /api/seasonal/cycle.
title: Seasonal System Acceptance Test

body: NON-NEGOTIABLE / TOP PRIORITY. Do not generalize this requirement into 'watch proven sellers.' The specifically named anchor is MJsOffTheHookDesigns. Canonical owner-supplied shop URL: https://www.etsy.com/ca/shop/MJsOffTheHookDesigns?ref=shop_profile&listing;_id=1825269747 . The shorter canonical shop route may also be stored, but the owner-supplied URL must remain in the benchmark registry and acceptance evidence.
note: the owner-supplied URL is stored verbatim, including its query string, and surfaces unchanged on /api/mjs where acceptance evidence is read from. mission.check_report() refuses a report naming any other shop, which is the mechanical form of 'do not generalize this into watch proven sellers'.
title: OWNER MANDATE - MJsOffTheHookDesigns Is the Named Priority Benchmark

body: Maintain dedicated MJs intelligence capacity independent of generic market research. Agent count is elastic and uncapped by an arbitrary small number: the orchestrator may fan out into very large logical specialist swarms when needed for complete catalogue coverage, image analysis, category decomposition, seasonal response and QA. Scale is justified by coverage/quality/latency and remains under global spend controls.
note: intel/capacity.py reserves a floor generic research cannot draw below and names what borrowing would starve; above it scale is bounded by spend rather than headcount and must name coverage, quality or latency
title: MJs Mission Has Dedicated Capacity

body: Establish and maintain full discoverable MJs catalogue coverage. Every listing is assigned to specialist category pods and represented in the MJs Coverage Matrix. Track newly discovered/changed listings, product family, generic product type, silhouette/form, palette, seasonal positioning, visual merchandising mechanisms, visible pricing/promotion, gallery structure and dated evidence.
note: intel/market_map.py maps every observed listing across ten attributes and reports its own staleness. Live against the real catalogue on 2026-09-19: 438 listings, 2 unclassified, stored routing drift 0, twelve pods. market_map.gaps() and GET /api/mjs/coverage name the gaps rather than counting them, and observe.reclassify() keeps the stored catalogue on the current vocabulary without re-reading Etsy. Palette is closing by itself: the deep audit backfills up to 40 unread galleries a scan and stops when the backlog is empty. What remains is silhouette and merchandising mechanism, which are judgements about a photograph -- parked on browser_vision rather than inferred from the title, because a map that inferred them would look complete and be fiction.
title: MJs Catalogue Is a Living Market Map

body: For every accessible MJs listing selected for baseline or change audit, browser/vision workers traverse the accessible gallery and analyze each image as competitive evidence. Extract product form, proportions, generic construction cues visible from the finished item, colour/stripe/blocking logic, styling, model/product presentation, detail coverage, setting, thumbnail strategy and seasonal signals. This is not satisfied by text scraping or search-result thumbnails.
note: same as #209: the gallery is traversed and inventoried with Etsy's own colour statistics, and image-level judgement is queued rather than guessed.
title: MJs Listing Photos Must Be Visually Studied

body: MJs photography may be used as visual market/merchandising evidence, but Brambleloop must create its own listing photographs/renders with its own canonical model, scenes and composition assets. Do not download/recolour/edit an MJs photograph and publish it as Brambleloop creative.
note: enforced at asset provenance in gates/asset_truth.py, which is the only place a file's origin is stated: a source outside camera/twin/generator/designer is ASSET_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED, and provenance describing a downloaded, scraped, screenshotted or recoloured competitor image is ASSET_COMPETITOR_SOURCE. Both block publication.
title: Do Not Reproduce MJs Photo Assets

body: When MJs demonstrates demand in a broad/generic product arena - cardigan, sweater, stocking, blanket, ornament, bag, hat, coaster, decor or another category - the relevant Brambleloop pod MUST consider entering that same arena. It may preserve commercially useful generic characteristics visible from the finished product (e.g. cropped V-neck button cardigan, striped/color-blocked look, relaxed fit) while independently engineering the Brambleloop pattern.
note: intel/response.consider_arena() makes 'MUST consider' a recorded decision including a refusal, permits the generic characteristics of a finished object and refuses anything that only makes sense as a reference to the source
title: Same Proven Product Arena Is Mandatory to Consider

body: Every commercially meaningful MJs concept is evaluated against the rolling seasonal calendar. Ask how the broad product concept can speak to the NEXT season/holiday through colour palette, styling, trim, motif vocabulary, gift context, supporting accessories, bundles and merchandising. Christmas, Halloween, Easter and fall/winter/spring/summer are mandatory recurring lenses; other events are evidence-driven.
note: response.seasonalise() enumerates all eight mandatory lenses and reports a palette-only answer as the recolour it is
title: Seasonalize MJs-Proven Concepts

body: If MJs has a strong cropped striped cardigan listing, Brambleloop may deliberately compete with a cropped striped cardigan for the same broad buyer/search market and develop Christmas colourways such as forest/cranberry/cream/gold or other current seasonal palettes. Brambleloop independently engineers stitch counts, construction, grading and written instructions and generates Brambleloop-owned listing imagery.
note: the owner's Christmas cardigan example runs as a test fixture over #306 and #307 rather than as a special case in the code
title: Owner Example - Christmas Cardigan Response

body: MJs listing/new-change event -> specialist pod -> visual/text market decomposition -> demand/season fit -> seasonal colour/theme tournament -> customer make-time estimate -> preferred/latest launch date -> original CIR/pattern engineering -> truth/certification -> Brambleloop-owned premium assets -> benchmark challenge -> SEO/ads/content -> launch -> performance measurement -> winner scaling -> lessons back to MJs specialist memory.
note: response.PIPELINE names all fourteen stages and the gate each one must pass; a stage cannot run before its predecessor and a failed gate stops the run rather than marking it amber
title: MJs Trend-to-Season Mission Pipeline

body: MJs-inspired competitive responses must not arrive when the holiday starts. Work backward from the date customers want the FINISHED object. Include crochet make time, customer planning/purchase time, testing/QA, marketplace discovery/indexing, creative iteration and paid-ad learning. Complex garments/blankets receive materially more runway than quick ornaments/coasters.
note: the whole backward chain exists for this: complex garments and blankets receive materially more runway than ornaments because make time is a term in the subtraction. Measured against the generated catalogue on 2026-09-18: Canadian Thanksgiving is already missed for all eleven, and the largest piece's preferred Christmas launch is 2026-09-27.
title: Release Ahead of the Customer's Making Window

body: Continuously calculate days remaining to preferred and latest viable launch for every MJs-derived seasonal opportunity. Escalate at-risk opportunities, reallocate agents, simplify only when product truth permits, or defer to next season when the customer can no longer reasonably finish the project in time.
note: seasonal.sentinel runs daily, separates at-risk from merely past-preferred, and raises a correlated P2 only for windows where reallocating effort still changes the outcome -- a missed window is not an incident, because #297 already decided what happens to those and an incident per missed product per day trains everyone to ignore the channel.
title: MJs Seasonal Deadline Sentinel

body: At minimum maintain MJs-aware specialist capability for garments/clothing, blankets/throws, stockings, ornaments/tree decor, home/decor, bags/accessories, hats/wearables and seasonal/gift products, adding new pods as catalogue evidence requires. Each pod owns benchmark history, seasonal opportunity map, quality rubric, Brambleloop coverage and improvement experiments.
note: the eight named pods are permanent constants with rubrics: garments, blankets, stockings, ornaments, home_decor, bags, hats, seasonal_gift, plus a visible 'unclassified' queue so an unrecognised listing is never nudged into the nearest pod. New pods are added; none is pruned for a quiet quarter.
title: MJs Category Pods Are Permanent

body: After full baseline, perform frequent lightweight checks for catalogue/listing changes and immediately deep-audit new or materially changed listings. Adapt cadence to MJs observed release behavior and seasonal urgency. The goal is fast awareness without repeatedly paying to reprocess identical content.
note: frequent lightweight checks with adaptive cadence, and a changed listing triggers an immediate deep re-audit. Cost stays bounded because an unchanged listing opens no galleries.
title: MJs Change Detection Is High Priority

body: Every meaningful MJs product arena lacking a competitive Brambleloop response enters a prioritized gap queue scored by apparent demand, seasonal timing, search opportunity, make-time, expected contribution, creative potential and portfolio fit. The queue must distinguish 'uncovered', 'concepting', 'engineering', 'certified', 'launched', 'validated winner' and 'not pursuing + reason'.
note: intel/coverage.py holds the gap queue with all seven states the requirement names, a transition table that refuses a state the work did not pass through, and a mandatory reason for not_pursuing. Scored on the seven named components, each stored beside the score with the share of the weighting actually answered, so a confident number computed from one component cannot pass for a considered one.
title: MJs Coverage Gap Queue

body: For relevant products, compare Brambleloop's finished offer against category-matched current MJs evidence on product desirability, visual appeal, thumbnail strength, fit/proportion where applicable, seasonal relevance, pattern deliverables, clarity, value, trust and merchandising. If Brambleloop is visibly generic/amateur or materially weaker, return it to development.
note: MJs quality challenge; needs MJs evidence
title: MJs Quality Challenge Is Release-Blocking

body: All observations, Brambleloop launches, failures, owner vetoes, conversion data and customer outcomes update the MJs specialist pods' versioned learning memory. Challenger agents should repeatedly test better ways to interpret MJs market signals, generate stronger seasonal responses and improve commercial execution.
note: intel/memory.py versions every pod interpretation, moves standing only on recorded outcomes and refuses repetition as evidence; challengers win on outcomes or not at all, and superseded lessons are kept
title: MJs Mission Feeds Continuous Improvement

body: When the owner purchases approximately ten representative MJs patterns, treat them as a controlled customer-experience benchmark set: analyze organization, navigation, terminology, sizing presentation, charting, video/support integration, materials, troubleshooting and overall deliverable quality. Use lessons to improve Brambleloop's own independently created products. Do not reproduce protected pattern text/charts/instructions.
